KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Targeted accuracy during the refinement iteration.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_IRAC_QUICK_EXIT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Only one extra refinement iteration is done when the norm is below this value.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_IRAC_SWITCH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The algorithm switches to the polynomial refinement when the norm is below this value.

KEYWORD.NAME: ON_THE_FLY_LOC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: On the fly localization of the molecular orbitals. Can only be used with OT/IRAC.

KEYWORD.NAME: MINIMIZER

ITEM.NAME: SD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Steepest descent: not recommended

ITEM.NAME: CG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Conjugate Gradients: most reliable, use for difficult systems. The total energy should decrease at every OT CG step if the line search is appropriate.

ITEM.NAME: DIIS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct inversion in the iterative subspace: less reliable than CG, but sometimes about 50% faster

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing approximating the inverse Hessian

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimizer to be used with the OT method

KEYWORD.NAME: SAFE_DIIS
SAFER_DIIS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Reject DIIS steps if they point away from the minimum, do SD in that case.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_HISTORY_VEC
NDIIS
N_DIIS
N_BROYDEN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of history vectors to be used with DIIS or BROYDEN

KEYWORD.NAME: BROYDEN_SIGMA_DECREASE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Reduction of curvature on bad approximation.

KEYWORD.NAME: LINESEARCH
LINE_SEARCH

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: take fixed length steps

ITEM.NAME: 2PNT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: extrapolate based on 2 points

ITEM.NAME: 3PNT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: ... or on 3 points

ITEM.NAME: GOLD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: perform 1D golden section search of the minimum (very expensive)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: 1D line search algorithm to be used with the OT minimizer, in increasing order of robustness and cost. MINIMIZER CG combined with LINESEARCH GOLD should always find an electronic minimum. Whereas the 2PNT minimizer is almost always OK, 3PNT might be needed for systems in which successive OT CG steps do not decrease the total energy.

KEYWORD.NAME: STEPSIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial stepsize used for the line search, sometimes this parameter can be reduced to stabilize DIIS or to improve the CG behavior in the first few steps. The optimal value depends on the quality of the preconditioner. A negative values leaves the choice to CP2K depending on the preconditioner.

KEYWORD.NAME: GOLD_TARGET
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Target relative uncertainty in the location of the minimum for LINESEARCH GOLD

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECONDITIONER

ITEM.NAME: FULL_ALL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Most effective state selective preconditioner based on diagonalization, requires the ENERGY_GAP parameter to be an underestimate of the HOMO-LUMO gap. This preconditioner is recommended for almost all systems, except very large systems where make_preconditioner would dominate the total computational cost.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Based on H-eS cholesky inversion, similar to FULL_SINGLE in preconditioning efficiency but cheaper to construct, might be somewhat less robust. Recommended for large systems.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SINGLE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Based on H-eS diagonalisation, not as good as FULL_ALL, but somewhat cheaper to apply.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_KINETIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky inversion of S and T, fast construction, robust, and relatively good, use for very large systems.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_S_INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky inversion of S, not as good as FULL_KINETIC, yet equally expensive.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: skip preconditioning

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of preconditioner to be used with all minimization schemes. They differ in effectiveness, cost of construction, cost of application. Properly preconditioned minimization can be orders of magnitude faster than doing nothing.

KEYWORD.NAME: CHOLESKY

ITEM.NAME: OFF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The cholesky algorithm is not used

ITEM.NAME: REDUCE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Reduce is called

ITEM.NAME: RESTORE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Reduce is replaced by two restore

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Restore uses operator multiply by inverse of the triangular matrix

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_DBCSR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Like inverse, but matrix stored as dbcsr, sparce matrix algebra used when possible

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If FULL_ALL the cholesky decomposition of the S matrix is used. Options on the algorithm to be used.

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECOND_SOLVER

ITEM.NAME: DEFAULT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: the default

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by triangular solve (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_CHOLESKY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by explicit inversion (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_UPDATE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Performs a Hotelling update of the inverse if a previous preconditioner is present. Mainly useful for GPU accelerated systems (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How the preconditioner is applied to the residual.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should be an estimate for the energy gap [a.u.] (HOMO-LUMO) and is used in preconditioning, especially effective with the FULL_ALL preconditioner, in which case it should be an underestimate of the gap (can be a small number, e.g. 0.002). FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE takes it as lower bound (values below 0.05 can cause stability issues). In general, higher values will tame the preconditioner in case of poor initial guesses. A negative value will leave the choice to CP2K depending on type of preconditioner.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_TAYLOR
EPSTAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Target accuracy of the taylor expansion for the matrix functions, should normally be kept as is.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_TAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum order of the Taylor expansion before diagonalisation is preferred, for large parallel runs a slightly higher order could sometimes result in a small speedup.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROTATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Introduce additional variables so that rotations of the occupied subspace are allowed as well, only needed for cases where the energy is not invariant under a rotation of the occupied subspace such as non-singlet restricted calculations or fractional occupations.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Optimize orbital energies for use in Fermi-Dirac smearing (requires ROTATION and FD smearing to be active).

KEYWORD.NAME: OCCUPATION_PRECONDITIONER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preconditioner with the occupation numbers (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NONDIAG_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Add a non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NONDIAG_ENERGY_STRENGTH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The prefactor for the non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

However, it needs a pre-converged wavefunction obtained by at least one real diagonalization which is further optimized while keeping the original eigenvalue spectrum. The MO eigenvalues are NOT updated. The method might be useful to speed up calculations for large systems e.g. using a semi-empirical method.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_ADAPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Required accuracy in iterative diagonalization as compared to current SCF convergence

ITEM.NAME: FULL_ALL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Most effective state selective preconditioner based on diagonalization, requires the ENERGY_GAP parameter to be an underestimate of the HOMO-LUMO gap. This preconditioner is recommended for almost all systems, except very large systems where make_preconditioner would dominate the total computational cost.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Based on H-eS cholesky inversion, similar to FULL_SINGLE in preconditioning efficiency but cheaper to construct, might be somewhat less robust. Recommended for large systems.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SINGLE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Based on H-eS diagonalisation, not as good as FULL_ALL, but somewhat cheaper to apply.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_KINETIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky inversion of S and T, fast construction, robust, and relatively good, use for very large systems.

ITEM.NAME: FULL_S_INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky inversion of S, not as good as FULL_KINETIC, yet equally expensive.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: skip preconditioning

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of preconditioner to be used with all minimization schemes. They differ in effectiveness, cost of construction, cost of application. Properly preconditioned minimization can be orders of magnitude faster than doing nothing.

KEYWORD.NAME: CHOLESKY

ITEM.NAME: OFF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The cholesky algorithm is not used

ITEM.NAME: REDUCE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Reduce is called

ITEM.NAME: RESTORE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Reduce is replaced by two restore

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Restore uses operator multiply by inverse of the triangular matrix

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_DBCSR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Like inverse, but matrix stored as dbcsr, sparce matrix algebra used when possible

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If FULL_ALL the cholesky decomposition of the S matrix is used. Options on the algorithm to be used.

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECOND_SOLVER

ITEM.NAME: DEFAULT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: the default

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by triangular solve (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_CHOLESKY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by explicit inversion (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_UPDATE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Performs a Hotelling update of the inverse if a previous preconditioner is present. Mainly useful for GPU accelerated systems (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How the preconditioner is applied to the residual.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should be an estimate for the energy gap [a.u.] (HOMO-LUMO) and is used in preconditioning, especially effective with the FULL_ALL preconditioner, in which case it should be an underestimate of the gap (can be a small number, e.g. 0.002). FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE takes it as lower bound (values below 0.05 can cause stability issues). In general, higher values will tame the preconditioner in case of poor initial guesses. A negative value will leave the choice to CP2K depending on type of preconditioner.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_TAYLOR
EPSTAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Target accuracy of the taylor expansion for the matrix functions, should normally be kept as is.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_TAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum order of the Taylor expansion before diagonalisation is preferred, for large parallel runs a slightly higher order could sometimes result in a small speedup.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROTATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Introduce additional variables so that rotations of the occupied subspace are allowed as well, only needed for cases where the energy is not invariant under a rotation of the occupied subspace such as non-singlet restricted calculations or fractional occupations.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Optimize orbital energies for use in Fermi-Dirac smearing (requires ROTATION and FD smearing to be active).

KEYWORD.NAME: OCCUPATION_PRECONDITIONER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preconditioner with the occupation numbers (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NONDIAG_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Add a non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NONDIAG_ENERGY_STRENGTH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The prefactor for the non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NKRYLOV
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Dimension of the Krylov space used for the Lanczos refinement

KEYWORD.NAME: NBLOCK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Size of the block of vectors refined simultaneously by the Lanczos procedure

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_STD_DIAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Level of convergence to be reached before starting the Lanczos procedure. Above this threshold a standard diagonalization method is used. If negative Lanczos is started at the first iteration

KEYWORD.NAME: CHECK_MOS_CONV
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This requires to check the convergence of MOS also when standard diagonalization steps are performed, if the block krylov approach is active.

SECTION.NAME: DIAG_SUB_SCF
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Activation of self-consistenf subspace refinement by diagonalization of H by adjusting the occupation but keeping the MOS unchanged.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: controls the activation of inner SCF loop to refine occupations in MOS subspace

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of iterations for the SCF inner loop

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_ENE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Required energy accuracy for convergence of subspace diagonalization

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_ADAPT_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Required density matrix accuracy as compared to current SCF convergence

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SKIP_SUB_DIAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Level of convergence to be reached before starting the internal loop of subspace rotations. Above this threshold only the outer diagonalization method is used. If negative the subspace rotation is started at the first iteration

SECTION.NAME: MIXING
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define type and parameters for mixing procedures to be applied to the density matrix. Normally, only one type of mixing method should be accepted. The mixing procedures activated by this section are only active for diagonalization methods and linear scaling SCF, i.e. not with minimization methods based on OT.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the mixing procedure

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No mixing is applied

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_P_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct mixing of new and old density matrices

ITEM.NAME: KERKER_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mixing of the potential in reciprocal space using the Kerker damping

ITEM.NAME: PULAY_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Pulay mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING_NEW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing second version

ITEM.NAME: MULTISECANT_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Multisecant scheme for mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be included

KEYWORD.NAME: BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Denominator parameter in Kerker damping introduced to suppress charge sloshing: rho_mix(g) = rho_in(g) + alpha*g^2/(g^2 + beta^2)*(rho_out(g)-rho_in(g))

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be added to the Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of residual contribution to be added to Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: NMIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal number of density mixing (should be greater than 0), before starting DIIS

KEYWORD.NAME: NBUFFER
NPULAY
NBROYDEN
NMULTISECANT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous steps stored for the actual mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: BROY_W0
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: w0 parameter used in Broyden mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: REGULARIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Regularization parameter to stabilize the inversion of the residual matrix {Yn^t Yn} in the multisecant mixing scheme (noise)

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_STEP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Upper bound for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: R_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Control factor for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: NSKIP
NSKIP_MIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of initial iteration for which the mixing is skipped

KEYWORD.NAME: N_SIMPLE_MIX
NSIMPLEMIX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of kerker damping iterations before starting other mixing procedures

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_GVEC_EXP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restricts the G-space mixing to lower part of G-vector spectrum, up to a G0, by assigning the exponent of the Gaussian that can be represented by vectors smaller than G0 within a certain accuracy.

KEYWORD.NAME: GMIX_P
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Activate the mixing of the density matrix, using the same mixing coefficient applied for the g-space mixing.

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECONDITIONER

ITEM.NAME: FULL_ALL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Most effective state selective preconditioner based on diagonalization

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Based on H-eS cholesky inversion, similar to FULL_SINGLE in preconditioning efficiency but cheaper to construct, might be somewhat less robust. Recommended for large systems.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: skip preconditioning

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of preconditioner to be used with all minimization schemes.

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECOND_SOLVER

ITEM.NAME: DEFAULT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: the default

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by triangular solve (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

ITEM.NAME: INVERSE_CHOLESKY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky decomposition followed by explicit inversion (works for FULL_KINETIC/SINGLE_INVERSE/S_INVERSE)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How the preconditioner is applied to the residual.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should be an estimate for the energy gap [a.u.] (HOMO-LUMO) and is used in preconditioning, especially effective with the FULL_ALL preconditioner, in which case it should be an underestimate of the gap (0.001 doing normally fine). For the other preconditioners, making this value larger (0.2) will tame the preconditioner in case of poor initial guesses.

KEYWORD.NAME: NEW_PREC_EACH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of SCF iterations after which a new Preconditioner is computed

KEYWORD.NAME: FIRST_PREC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: First SCF iteration at which a Preconditioner is employed

KEYWORD.NAME: CONV_MOS_PERCENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal percent of MOS that have to converge within the Davidson loop before the SCF iteration is completed and a new Hamiltonian is computed

KEYWORD.NAME: SPARSE_MOS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use MOS as sparse matrix and avoid as much as possible multiplications with full matrices

KEYWORD.NAME: FILTER_TEMPERATURE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Temperature used for the filter function used to construct the filter matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: AUTO_CUTOFF_SCALE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scalar constant multiplied to maximum orbital size of each atom, used for automatically creating cutoff radii for atomic matrices

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Default tolerance used in generating the filter matrix. Anything less than EPS_FB will be regarded as zero

KEYWORD.NAME: COLLECTIVE_COMMUNICATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If set to TRUE, then all MPI communications required for the construction of the filter matrix is done at the start and end of each filter matrix calculation. This makes communications more efficient, at the expense of using more memory. If you find the fb_fltrmat_add_blkcol_mpi times at the end of CP2K output is high, then run again with this option set to .TRUE.

SECTION.NAME: OUTER_SCF
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: parameters controlling the outer SCF loop

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: controls the activation of the outer SCF loop

KEYWORD.NAME: TYPE

ITEM.NAME: DDAPC_CONSTRAINT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Enforce a constraint on the DDAPC, requires the corresponding section

ITEM.NAME: S2_CONSTRAINT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Enforce a constraint on the S2, requires the corresponding section

ITEM.NAME: BASIS_CENTER_OPT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Optimize positions of basis functions, if atom types FLOATING_BASIS_CENTER are defined

ITEM.NAME: CDFT_CONSTRAINT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Enforce a constraint on a generic CDFT weight population. Requires the corresponding section QS&CDFT which determines the type of weight used.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do nothing in the outer loop, useful for resetting the inner loop,

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies which kind of outer SCF should be employed

KEYWORD.NAME: OPTIMIZER

ITEM.NAME: SD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Takes steps in the direction of the gradient, multiplied by step_size

ITEM.NAME: DIIS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Uses a Direct Inversion in the Iterative Subspace method

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do nothing, useful only with the none type

ITEM.NAME: BISECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Bisection of the gradient, useful for difficult one dimensional cases

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden's method. Variant defined in BROYDEN_TYPE.

ITEM.NAME: NEWTON
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Newton's method. Only compatible with CDFT constraints.

ITEM.NAME: SECANT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Secant method. Only for one dimensional cases. See Broyden for multidimensional cases.

ITEM.NAME: NEWTON_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Newton's method with backtracking line search to find the optimal step size. Only compatible with CDFT constraints. Starts from the regular Newton solution and successively reduces the step size until the L2 norm of the CDFT gradient decreases or MAX_LS steps is reached. Potentially very expensive because each iteration performs a full SCF calculation.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method used to bring the outer loop to a stationary point

KEYWORD.NAME: BISECT_TRUST_COUNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of times the same point will be used in bisection, a small number guards against the effect of wrongly converged states.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The target gradient of the outer SCF variables. Notice that the EPS_SCF of the inner loop also determines the value that can be reached in the outer loop, typically EPS_SCF of the outer loop must be smaller than or equal to EPS_SCF of the inner loop.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIIS_BUFFER_LENGTH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of DIIS vectors used

KEYWORD.NAME: EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of past states used in the extrapolation of the variables during e.g. MD

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The maximum number of outer loops

KEYWORD.NAME: STEP_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The initial step_size used in the optimizer (currently steepest descent). Note that in cases where a sadle point is sought for (constrained DFT), this can be negative. For Newton and Broyden optimizers, use a value less/higher than the default 1.0 (in absolute value, the sign is not significant) to active an under/overrelaxed optimizer.

SECTION.NAME: CDFT_OPT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters controlling optimization methods that are compatible only with CDFT based constraints (i.e. CDFT SCF is active). Specifically, the control parameters for the Broyden and Newton optimizers are defined in this section.

KEYWORD.NAME: BROYDEN_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: BT1
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden's first method, also known as the good method. The initial Jacobian is built from MD history if available. Otherwise switches to SD for one SCF iteration until a Jacobian can be built from the SCF history.

ITEM.NAME: BT1_EXPLICIT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but computes the explicit Jacobian with finite differences. Requires a CDFT SCF procedure to be active.

ITEM.NAME: BT2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but uses Broyden's second method, also known as the bad method.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_EXPLICIT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1_EXPLICIT, but using Broyden's second method.

ITEM.NAME: BT1_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size (see optimizer NEWTON_LS).

ITEM.NAME: BT1_EXPLICIT_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1_EXPLICIT, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT2, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_EXPLICIT_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT2_EXPLICIT, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the Broyden optimizer variant to use.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: FD1
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order forward difference (one extra energy evaluation per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD1_BACKWARD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order backward difference (one extra energy evaluation per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Second order forward difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD2_BACKWARD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Second order backward difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD1_CENTRAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order central difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Finite difference method used to calculate the inverse Jacobian needed by some optimizers. Compatible only with CDFT constraints.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_STEP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Step size to use in the calculation of the inverse Jacobian with finite differences. Expects one value for all constraints, or one value per constraint.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_FREQ
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines parameters that control how often the explicit Jacobian is built, which is needed by some optimizers. Expects two values. The first value determines how many consecutive CDFT SCF iterations should skip a rebuild, whereas the latter how many MD steps. The values can be zero (meaning never rebuild) or positive. Both values cannot be zero.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restart the inverse Jacobian using the vector defined with keyword JACOBIAN_VECTOR.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_VECTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the inverse Jacobian matrix. Useful for restarting calculations. Expects n^2 values where n is the total number of constraints. The matrix should be given in row major order.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The maximum number of backtracking line search steps to perform.

KEYWORD.NAME: FACTOR_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Control parameter for backtracking line search. The step size is reduced by this factor on every line search iteration. Value must be between 0 and 1 (exclusive).

KEYWORD.NAME: CONTINUE_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Continue backtracking line search until MAX_LS steps are reached or the norm of the CDFT gradient no longer decreases. Default (false) behavior exits the line search procedure on the first step that the gradient decreases.

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: BACKUP_COPIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the maximum number of backup copies.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: BACKUP_COPIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the maximum number of backup copies.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: LS_SCF
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the parameters of the linear scaling SCF routines

KEYWORD.NAME: LS_DIIS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Perform DIIS within linear scaling SCF

KEYWORD.NAME: INI_DIIS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration cycle to start DIIS Kohn-Sham matrix update

KEYWORD.NAME: NMIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal number of density mixing before start DIIS

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_DIIS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold on the convergence to start using DIIS

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of SCF iteration to be performed for one optimization

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Target accuracy for the SCF convergence in terms of change of the total energy per electron.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIXING_FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Mixing density matrices uses the specified fraction in the SCF procedure.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold used for filtering matrix operations.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Value (or initial guess) for the chemical potential, i.e. some suitable energy between HOMO and LUMO energy.

KEYWORD.NAME: FIXED_MU
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should the calculation be performed at fixed chemical potential, or should it be found fixing the number of electrons

KEYWORD.NAME: EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous matrices used for the ASPC extrapolation of the initial guess. 0 implies that an atomic guess is used at each step. low (1-2) will result in a drift of the constant of motion during MD. high (>5) might be somewhat unstable, leading to more SCF iterations.

KEYWORD.NAME: S_PRECONDITIONER

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No preconditioner

ITEM.NAME: ATOMIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using atomic blocks

ITEM.NAME: MOLECULAR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using molecular sub-blocks. Recommended if molecules are defined and not too large.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preconditions S with some appropriate form.

KEYWORD.NAME: S_SQRT_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: NEWTONSCHULZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using a Newton-Schulz-like iteration

ITEM.NAME: PROOT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using the p-th root method.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method for the caclulation of the sqrt of S.

KEYWORD.NAME: S_SQRT_ORDER
SIGN_SQRT_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Order of the iteration method for the calculation of the sqrt of S.

KEYWORD.NAME: PURIFICATION_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: SIGN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Sign matrix iteration.

ITEM.NAME: TRS4
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Trace resetting 4th order scheme

ITEM.NAME: TC2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Trace conserving 2nd order scheme

ITEM.NAME: PEXSI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: PEXSI method

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scheme used to purify the Kohn-Sham matrix into the density matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: SIGN_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: NEWTONSCHULZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Newton-Schulz iteration.

ITEM.NAME: PROOT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: p-th order root iteration

ITEM.NAME: SUBMATRIX
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Submatrix method

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method used for the computation of the sign matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: SUBMATRIX_SIGN_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: NEWTONSCHULZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Newton-Schulz iteration.

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct method calculating all eigenvalues.

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_MUADJ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct method with internal adjustment of mu

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_MUADJ_LOWMEM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct method with internal adjustment of mu, using two passes to save memory

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method used for the computation of the sign matrix of all submatrices.

KEYWORD.NAME: SIGN_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Order of the method used for the computation of the sign matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: SIGN_SYMMETRIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use symmetric orthogonalization when generating the input for the sign function.

KEYWORD.NAME: DYNAMIC_THRESHOLD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should the threshold for the purification be chosen dynamically

KEYWORD.NAME: NON_MONOTONIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should the purification be performed non-monotonically. Relevant for TC2 only.

KEYWORD.NAME: MATRIX_CLUSTER_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: ATOMIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using atomic blocks

ITEM.NAME: MOLECULAR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using molecular blocks.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify how atomic blocks should be clustered in the used matrices, in order to improve flop rate, and possibly speedup the matrix multiply. Note that the atomic s_preconditioner can not be used. Furthermore, since screening is on matrix blocks, slightly more accurate results can be expected with molecular.

KEYWORD.NAME: RESTART_WRITE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the density matrix at the end of the SCF (currently requires EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER>0). Files might be rather large.

KEYWORD.NAME: RESTART_READ
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Read the density matrix before the (first) SCF.

KEYWORD.NAME: S_INVERSION

ITEM.NAME: SIGN_SQRT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using the inverse sqrt as obtained from sign function iterations.

ITEM.NAME: HOTELLING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using the Hotellign iteration.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method used to compute the inverse of S.

KEYWORD.NAME: REPORT_ALL_SPARSITIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Run the sparsity report at the end of the SCF

KEYWORD.NAME: PERFORM_MU_SCAN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Do a scan of the chemical potential after the SCF

KEYWORD.NAME: CHECK_S_INV
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Perform an accuracy check on the inverse/sqrt of the s matrix.

SECTION.NAME: CURVY_STEPS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the parameters of the linear scaling SCF routines

KEYWORD.NAME: LINE_SEARCH

ITEM.NAME: 3POINT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Performs a three point line search

ITEM.NAME: 3POINT_2D
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Only for spin unrestricted calcualtions. Separate step sizes for alpha and beta spin using a fit to a 2D parabolic function

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Line serch type used in the curvy_setp optimization.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_BCH_HISTORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of stored matrices in the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff series. Reduces the BCH evaluation during line search but can be memory intense.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_HESSIAN_SHIFT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal eigenvalue shift for the Hessian in the Newton iteration. Useful for small band gap systems (0.5-1.0 recommended).

KEYWORD.NAME: FILTER_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Allows to set a separate EPS_FILTER in the newton iterations. The new EPS is EPS_FILTER*FILTER_FACTOR.

KEYWORD.NAME: FILTER_FACTOR_SCALE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Allows for dynamic EPS_FILTER. Updates the filter factor every SCF-Newton step by FILTER_FACTOR=FILTER_FACTOR*FILTER_FACTOR_SCALE

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_FILTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Lowest EPS_FILTER in dynamic filtering. Given as multiple of EPS_FILTER: EPS_FILTER_MIN=EPS_FILTER*MIN_FILTER

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the parameters needed for the chebyshev expansion based properties.

SECTION.NAME: RHO_MIXING
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define type and parameters for mixing procedures to be applied to the density matrix. Normally, only one type of mixing method should be accepted. The mixing procedures activated by this section are only active for diagonalization methods and linear scaling SCF, i.e. not with minimization methods based on OT.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the mixing procedure

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No mixing is applied

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_P_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct mixing of new and old density matrices

ITEM.NAME: KERKER_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mixing of the potential in reciprocal space using the Kerker damping

ITEM.NAME: PULAY_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Pulay mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING_NEW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing second version

ITEM.NAME: MULTISECANT_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Multisecant scheme for mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be included

KEYWORD.NAME: BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Denominator parameter in Kerker damping introduced to suppress charge sloshing: rho_mix(g) = rho_in(g) + alpha*g^2/(g^2 + beta^2)*(rho_out(g)-rho_in(g))

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be added to the Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of residual contribution to be added to Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: NMIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal number of density mixing (should be greater than 0), before starting DIIS

KEYWORD.NAME: NBUFFER
NPULAY
NBROYDEN
NMULTISECANT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous steps stored for the actual mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: BROY_W0
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: w0 parameter used in Broyden mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: REGULARIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Regularization parameter to stabilize the inversion of the residual matrix {Yn^t Yn} in the multisecant mixing scheme (noise)

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_STEP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Upper bound for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: R_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Control factor for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: NSKIP
NSKIP_MIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of initial iteration for which the mixing is skipped

KEYWORD.NAME: N_SIMPLE_MIX
NSIMPLEMIX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of kerker damping iterations before starting other mixing procedures

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_GVEC_EXP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restricts the G-space mixing to lower part of G-vector spectrum, up to a G0, by assigning the exponent of the Gaussian that can be represented by vectors smaller than G0 within a certain accuracy.

KEYWORD.NAME: GMIX_P
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Activate the mixing of the density matrix, using the same mixing coefficient applied for the g-space mixing.

SECTION.NAME: PEXSI
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the parameters of the PEXSI library. The density matrix is calculated with PEXSI if PURIFICATION_METHOD (in LS_SCF section) is set to PEXSI. The computational cost of PEXSI is at most quadratically scaling w.r.t. the system size and PEXSI is applicable to insulating and metallic systems. The value of EPS_PGF_ORB (in QS input section) defines the sparsity of the matrices sent to PEXSI and EPS_FILTER is overwritten with 0.

KEYWORD.NAME: GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Spectral gap. Note: This can be set to be 0 in most cases.

KEYWORD.NAME: NUM_POLE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of terms in the pole expansion (should be even).

KEYWORD.NAME: IS_INERTIA_COUNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether inertia counting is used each time the DFT driver of PEXSI is invoked. If FALSE, inertia counting is still used in the first SCF iteration.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_PEXSI_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of PEXSI iterations after each inertia counting procedure.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU_MIN_0
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial guess of lower bound for mu.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU_MAX_0
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial guess of upper bound for mu.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU_INERTIA_TOLERANCE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Stopping criterion in terms of the chemical potential for the inertia counting procedure.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU_INERTIA_EXPANSION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the chemical potential is not in the initial interval, the interval is expanded by MU_INERTIA_EXPANSION.

KEYWORD.NAME: MU_PEXSI_SAFE_GUARD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Safe guard criterion in terms of the chemical potential to reinvoke the inertia counting procedure.

KEYWORD.NAME: NUM_ELECTRON_PEXSI_TOLERANCE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Stopping criterion of the PEXSI iteration in terms of The number of electrons compared to the exact number of electrons. This threshold is the target tolerance applied at convergence of SCF.

KEYWORD.NAME: NUM_ELECTRON_INITIAL_TOLERANCE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The same as NUM_ELECTRON_PEXSI_TOLERANCE but applied in the first SCF steps. If set to a value smaller than NUM_ELECTRON_PEXSI_TOLERANCE, it is overwritten with NUM_ELECTRON_PEXSI_TOLERANCE (default). If set to a value larger than NUM_ELECTRON_PEXSI_TOLERANCE, the PEXSI tolerance in number of electrons is set adaptively according to the SCF convergence error of the previous SCF step. This reduces the number of PEXSI iterations in the first SCF steps but leads to at least one more SCF step.

KEYWORD.NAME: ORDERING

ITEM.NAME: PARALLEL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Parallel ordering using ParMETIS/PT-SCOTCH (PARMETIS option in SuperLU_DIST)

ITEM.NAME: SEQUENTIAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Sequential ordering using METIS (METIS_AT_PLUS_A option in SuperLU_DIST)

ITEM.NAME: MULTIPLE_MINIMUM_DEGREE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Multiple minimum degree ordering (MMD_AT_PLUS_A option in SuperLU_DIST)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Ordering strategy for factorization and selected inversion.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROW_ORDERING

ITEM.NAME: NOROWPERM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No row permutation (NOROWPERM option in SuperLU_DIST)

ITEM.NAME: LARGEDIAG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Make diagonal entry larger than off diagonal (LargeDiag option in SuperLU_DIST)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: row permutation strategy for factorization and selected inversion.

KEYWORD.NAME: NP_SYMB_FACT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of processors for PARMETIS/PT-SCOTCH. Only used if ORDERING is set to PARALLEL. If 0, the number of processors for PARMETIS/PT-SCOTCH will be set equal to the number of MPI ranks per pole. Note: if more than one processor is used, a segmentation fault may occur in the symbolic factorization phase.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_RANKS_PER_POLE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The minimum number of processors used for each pole. The real number of processors per pole is the smallest number greater or equal to MIN_RANKS_PER_POLE that divides MPI size without remainder. For efficiency, MIN_RANKS_PER_POLE should be a small numbers (limited by the available memory).

KEYWORD.NAME: CSR_SCREENING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether distance screening should be applied to improve sparsity of CSR matrices.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Mixing fraction of new and old optimizied solutions.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_PAO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of PAO basis optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_CYCLES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of PAO line search cycles for a given hamiltonian.

ITEM.NAME: FOCK

ITEM.NAME: EXP

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: always take steps of fixed INITIAL_STEP_SIZE

SECTION.NAME: ALMO_SCF
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Settings for a class of efficient linear scaling methods based on absolutely localized orbitals (ALMOs). ALMO methods are currently restricted to closed-shell molecular systems.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold for the matrix sparsity filter

KEYWORD.NAME: ALMO_SCF_GUESS

ITEM.NAME: MOLECULAR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: SCF calculations on single molecules controlled by the regular SCF keywords outside ALMO options. This kind of calculation is expensive and only recommended if ALMO SCF does not converge from the ATOMIC guess.

ITEM.NAME: ATOMIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Superposition of atomic densities.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The method to generate initial ALMOs.

KEYWORD.NAME: MO_OVERLAP_INV_ALG

ITEM.NAME: LS_HOTELLING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Linear scaling iterative Hotelling algorithm. Fast for large sparse matrices.

ITEM.NAME: LS_TAYLOR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Linear scaling algorithm based on Taylor expansion of (A+B)^(-1).

ITEM.NAME: DENSE_CHOLESKY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Stable but dense Cholesky algorithm. Cubically scaling.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Algorithm to invert MO overlap matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALMO_EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous states used for the ASPC extrapolation of the ALMO initial guess. 0 implies that the guess is given by ALMO_SCF_GUESS at each step.

KEYWORD.NAME: XALMO_EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous states used for the ASPC extrapolation of the initial guess for the delocalization correction.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALMO_ALGORITHM

ITEM.NAME: DIAG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: DIIS-accelerated diagonalization controlled by ALMO_OPTIMIZER_DIIS. Recommended for large systems containing small fragments.

ITEM.NAME: PCG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Energy minimization with a PCG algorithm controlled by ALMO_OPTIMIZER_PCG.

ITEM.NAME: TRUST_REGION
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Trust-region optimizer is recommended if PCG has difficulty converging. It is controlled by ALMO_OPTIMIZER_TRUSTR

ITEM.NAME: SKIP
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Skip optimization of block-diagonal ALMOs.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the algorithm to update block-diagonal ALMOs during the SCF procedure.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Neglect electron delocalization

ITEM.NAME: XALMO_1DIAG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Correction based on one diagonalization of the spatially projected Hamiltonian (XALMO)

ITEM.NAME: XALMO_SCF

ITEM.NAME: FULL_X
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Single excitation correction (no Hamiltonian re-build) without spatial restrictions

ITEM.NAME: FULL_SCF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Self-consistent treatment of delocalization without spatial restrictions

ITEM.NAME: FULL_X_THEN_SCF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Single excitation correction followed by full SCF procedure, both without spatial restrictions

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Methods to reintroduce electron delocalization, which is excluded with the block-diagonal ALMO reference. Electron delocalization can be computed using either fully delocalized MOs or spatially restricted ALMOs (called eXtended ALMOs or XALMOs). All methods below use either a PCG or trust-region optimizers controlled by XALMO_OPTIMIZER_* subsections. The only exception is the non-iterative XALMO_1DIAG.

KEYWORD.NAME: XALMO_R_CUTOFF_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Controls the localization radius of XALMOs: R_cutoff = XALMO_R_CUTOFF_FACTOR*(radius(at1)+radius(at2))

KEYWORD.NAME: RETURN_ORTHOGONALIZED_MOS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Orthogonalize final ALMOs before they are returned to Quickstep (i.e. for calculation of properties)

KEYWORD.NAME: CONSTRUCT_NLMOS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Turns on post-SCF construction of NLMOs

SECTION.NAME: PENALTY
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Add penalty terms to the energy functional.

KEYWORD.NAME: OPERATOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of opertator which defines the spread functional

KEYWORD.NAME: PENALTY_STRENGTH_DECREASE_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Factor that decreases the strength of the orthogonalization penalty.

KEYWORD.NAME: DETERMINANT_TOLERANCE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Stop the optimization of the penalty strength if the determinant of the overlap changes less than this tolerance threshold.

KEYWORD.NAME: FINAL_DETERMINANT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The final determinant that obtained after optimization.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMPACTIFICATION_FILTER_START
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Set orbital coefficients with absolute value smaller than this value to zero.

SECTION.NAME: MATRIX_ITERATE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls linear scaling iterative procedure on matrices: inversion, sqrti, etc. High-order Lanczos accelerates convergence provided it can estimate the eigenspectrum correctly.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_TARGET_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Multiplication factor that determines acceptable error in the iterative procedure. Acceptable error = EPS_TARGET_FACTOR * EPS_FILTER

KEYWORD.NAME: ORDER_LANCZOS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Order of the Lanczos estimator. Use 0 to turn off. Do not use 1.

SECTION.NAME: ANALYSIS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls electronic structure analysis based on ALMOs and XALMOs.

KEYWORD.NAME: FROZEN_MO_ENERGY_TERM

ITEM.NAME: SKIP
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not compute the frozen MO energy term.

ITEM.NAME: SUBLATTICE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use energies of single molecules in their positions in the crystal cell as the reference. This term does not have an interpretation if fragmetns are charged.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Perform calculations on single molecules to compute the frozen density term

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls printing of detailed ALMO decomosition analysis results

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: JUST_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for an ENERGY/ENERGY_FORCE calculation.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for POWELL based optimization steps.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Path integral md steps.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: SCREENING
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up screening parameters if requested

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCHWARZ
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the near field part of the electronic repulsion integrals using the Schwarz inequality for the given threshold.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCHWARZ_FORCES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the near field part of the electronic repulsion integrals using the Schwarz inequality for the given threshold. This will be approximately the accuracy of the forces, and should normally be similar to EPS_SCF

KEYWORD.NAME: SCREEN_P_FORCES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the electronic repulsion integrals for the forces using the density matrix. This results in a significant speedup for large systems, but might require a somewhat tigher EPS_SCHWARZ_FORCES.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCREEN_ON_INITIAL_P
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screen on an initial density matrix. For the first MD step this matrix must be provided by a Restart File.

KEYWORD.NAME: P_SCREEN_CORRECTION_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Recalculates integrals on the fly if the actual density matrix is larger by a given factor than the initial one. If the factor is set to 0.0_dp, this feature is disabled.

SECTION.NAME: MEMORY
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up memory parameters for the storage of the ERI's if requested

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_STORAGE_SCALING
EPS_STORAGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor to scale eps_schwarz. Storage threshold for compression will be EPS_SCHWARZ*EPS_STORAGE_SCALING.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_MEMORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the maximum amount of memory [MiB] to be consumed by the full HFX module. All temporary buffers and helper arrays are subtracted from this number. What remains will be used for storage of integrals. NOTE: This number is assumed to represent the memory available to one MPI process. When running a threaded version, cp2k automatically takes care of distributing the memory among all the threads within a process.

KEYWORD.NAME: STORAGE_LOCATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Loaction where ERI's are stored if MAX_DISK_SPACE /=0 Expects a path to a directory.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_DISK_SPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the maximum amount of disk space [MiB] used to store precomputed compressed four-center integrals. If 0, nothing is stored to disk

KEYWORD.NAME: TREAT_FORCES_IN_CORE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines whether the derivative ERI's should be stored to RAM or not. Only meaningful when performing Ehrenfest MD. Memory usage is defined via MAX_MEMORY, i.e. the memory is shared wit the energy ERI's.

SECTION.NAME: RI
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for RI method in HFX (experimental, forces not yet implemented).

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Filter threshold for DBCSR tensor contraction.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER_2C
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Filter threshold for 2c integrals. Default should be kept.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_STORAGE_SCALING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor to scale EPS_FILTER for storage of 3-center integrals. Storage threshold will be EPS_FILTER*EPS_STORAGE_SCALING.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER_MO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Filter threshold for contraction of 3-center integrals with MOs. Default should be kept.

KEYWORD.NAME: OMEGA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The range parameter for the short range operator (in 1/a0). Default is OMEGA from INTERACTION_POTENTIAL.

KEYWORD.NAME: CUTOFF_RADIUS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The cutoff radius (in Angstroms) for the truncated Coulomb operator. Default is CUTOFF_RADIUS from INTERACTION_POTENTIAL.

KEYWORD.NAME: KP_NGROUPS
NGROUPS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of MPI subgroup that work in parallel during the SCF. The default value is 1. Using N subgroups should speed up the calculation by a factor ~N, at the cost of N times more memory usage.

KEYWORD.NAME: KP_USE_DELTA_P
USE_DELTA_P
KP_USE_P_DIFF
USE_P_DIFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This kweyword controls whether the KS matrix at each SCF cycle is built by adding the contribution of the denisty difference (wrt to previous step) to the KS matrix of the previous step. As the SCF converges, the density fluctuations get smaller and sparsity increases, leading to faster SCF steps. Not always numerically stable => turn off if SCF struggles to converge.

KEYWORD.NAME: KP_STACK_SIZE
STACK_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: When doing contraction over periodic cells of the type: T_mu^a,nu^b,P^c = (mu^a nu^b | Q^d) * (Q^d | P^c), with a,b,c,d labeling cells, there are in principle Ncells contractions taking place. Because a smaller number of contractions involving larger tensors is more efficient, the tensors can be stacked along the d direction. STCK_SIZE controls the size of this stack. Larger stacks are more efficient, but required more memory.

KEYWORD.NAME: KP_RI_EXTENSION_FACTOR
RI_EXTENSION_FACTOR
RI_EXT
RI_EXT_FACT
KP_RI_EXT
KP_RI_EXT_FACT
KP_RI_BASIS_EXT
RI_BASIS_EXT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: In KP-RI-HFX, each atom has its own local RI basis. The RI basis is defined by a sphere of radius R centered on the atom, whereby all neighboring atoms within that sphere contribute their RI basis elements. The radius of that sphere is calculated based on the systems' most diffuse orbital PGF (with exponant alpha), such that EPS_PGF_ORB * KP_RI_EXTENSION_FACTOR = exp(-alpha*R^2). The default value of 1.0 is safe. More accurate results can be obtained with a value < 1.0, at greated computational cost.

KEYWORD.NAME: KP_RI_BUMP_FACTOR
RI_BUMP
BUMP
BUMP_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: In KP-RI-HFX, the extended RI basis set has a bump radius. All basis elements within that radius contribute with full weight. All basis elements beyond that radius have decaying weight, from 1 at the bump radius, to zero at the RI extension radius. The bump radius is calculated as a fraction of the RI extension radius: bump radius = KP_RI_NUMP_FACTOR * RI extension radius

KEYWORD.NAME: RI_METRIC

ITEM.NAME: HFX
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as HFX operator

ITEM.NAME: COULOMB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Standard Coulomb operator: 1/r

ITEM.NAME: IDENTITY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Overlap

ITEM.NAME: TRUNCATED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Truncated Coulomb operator: 1/r if (r<R_c), 0 otherwise

ITEM.NAME: SHORTRANGE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Short range: erfc(omega*r)/r

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The type of RI operator. Default is POTENTIAL_TYPE from INTERACTION_POTENTIAL. The standard Coulomb operator cannot be used in periodic systems.

KEYWORD.NAME: 2C_MATRIX_FUNCTIONS

ITEM.NAME: DIAG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Diagonalization with eigenvalue quenching: stable

ITEM.NAME: CHOLESKY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cholesky: not stable in case of ill-conditioned RI basis

ITEM.NAME: ITER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Iterative algorithms: linear scaling Hotelling's method for inverse and Newton-Schulz iteration for matrix square root

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Methods for matrix inverse and matrix square root.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_EIGVAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Throw away linear combinations of RI basis functions with a small eigenvalue, this is applied only if 2C_MATRIX_FUNCTIONS DIAG

KEYWORD.NAME: CHECK_2C_MATRIX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Report accuracy for the inverse/sqrt of the 2-center integral matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: CALC_COND_NUM
CALC_CONDITION_NUMBER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Calculate the condition number of integral matrices.

KEYWORD.NAME: SQRT_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Order of the iteration method for the calculation of the sqrt of 2-center integral matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_PGF_ORB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets precision of the integral tensors.

KEYWORD.NAME: RI_FLAVOR

ITEM.NAME: MO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: with MO coefficients

ITEM.NAME: RHO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: with density matrix

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Flavor of RI: how to contract 3-center integrals

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_BLOCK_SIZE_MO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum tensor block size for MOs.

KEYWORD.NAME: MEMORY_CUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Memory reduction factor. This keyword controls the batching of tensor contractions into smaller, more manageable chunks. The details vary depending on the RI_FLAVOR.

KEYWORD.NAME: FLAVOR_SWITCH_MEMORY_CUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Memory reduction factor to be applied upon RI_FLAVOR switching from MO to RHO. The RHO flavor typically requires more memory, and depending on the ressources available, a higher MEMORY_CUT.

SECTION.NAME: WF_CORRELATION
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up the wavefunction-based correlation methods as MP2, RI-MP2, RI-SOS-MP2, RI-RPA and GW (inside RI-RPA).

KEYWORD.NAME: MEMORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum allowed total memory usage during MP2 methods [MiB].

KEYWORD.NAME: E_GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Gap energy for integration grids in Hartree. Defaults to -1.0 (automatic determination). Recommended to set if several RPA or SOS-MP2 gradient calculations are requested or to be restarted. In this way, differences of integration grids across different runs are removed as CP2K does not include derivatives thereof.

KEYWORD.NAME: E_RANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Energy range (ratio of largest and smallest) energy difference of unoccupied and occupied orbitals for integration grids. Defaults to 0.0 (automatic determination). Recommended to set if several RPA or SOS-MP2 gradient calculations are requested or to be restarted. In this way, differences of integration grids across different runs are removed as CP2K does not include derivatives thereof.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCALE_S
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor of the singlet energy component (opposite spin, OS) of the MP2, RI-MP2 and SOS-MP2 correlation energy.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCALE_T
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor of the triplet energy component (same spin, SS) of the MP2 and RI-MP2 correlation energy.

KEYWORD.NAME: GROUP_SIZE
NUMBER_PROC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Group size used in the computation of GPW and MME integrals and the MP2 correlation energy. The group size must be a divisor of the total number of MPI ranks. A smaller group size (for example the number of MPI ranks per node) accelerates the computation of integrals but a too large group size increases communication costs. A too small group size may lead to out of memory.

KEYWORD.NAME: METHOD

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Skip MP2 calculation.

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_CANONICAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use the direct mp2 canonical approach.

ITEM.NAME: MP2_GPW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use the GPW approach to MP2.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method that is used to compute the MP2 energy.

KEYWORD.NAME: BIG_SEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Influencing the direct canonical MP2 method: Send big messages between processes (useful for >48 processors).

SECTION.NAME: RI_MP2
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters influencing the RI-MP2 method. RI-MP2 supports gradients.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Putting the &RI_MP2 section activates RI-MP2 calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: BLOCK_SIZE
MESSAGE_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines the blocking used for communication in RI-MP2. Larger BLOCK_SIZE reduces communication but requires more memory. The default (-1) is automatic.

KEYWORD.NAME: NUMBER_INTEGRATION_GROUPS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets the number of integration groups of the communication scheme in RI-MP2. Integrals will be replicated such that each integration group has all integrals available. Must be a divisor of the number of subgroups (see GROUP_SIZE keyword in the WF_CORRELATION section. Smaller groups reduce the communication costs but increase the memory developments. If the provided value is non-positive or not a divisor of the number of subgroups, the number of integration groups is determined automatically (default).

KEYWORD.NAME: PRINT_DGEMM_INFO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print details about all DGEMM calls.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Putting the &RI_RPA section activates RI-RPA calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: QUADRATURE_POINTS
RPA_NUM_QUAD_POINTS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of quadrature points for the numerical integration in the RI-RPA method.

KEYWORD.NAME: NUM_INTEG_GROUPS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of groups for the integration in the Laplace method. Each groups processes the same amount of quadrature points. It must be a divisor of the number of quadrature points and NUM_INTEG_GROUPS*GROUP_SIZE must be a divisor of the total number of processes. The default (-1) is automatic.

KEYWORD.NAME: MM_STYLE

ITEM.NAME: GEMM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use pdgemm: more flops, maybe faster.

ITEM.NAME: SYRK
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use pdysrk: fewer flops, maybe slower.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Matrix multiplication style for the Q matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: MINIMAX_QUADRATURE
MINIMAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use the Minimax quadrature scheme for performing the numerical integration. Maximum number of quadrature point limited to 20.

KEYWORD.NAME: RI_AXK
AXK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Decide whether to perform an RPA-AXK calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: RSE
SE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Decide whether to add singles correction.

KEYWORD.NAME: ADMM
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Decide whether to perform ADMM in the exact exchange calc. for RPA and/or GW. The ADMM XC correction is governed by the AUXILIARY_DENSITY_MATRIX_METHOD section in &DFT. In most cases, the Hartree-Fock exchange is not too expensive and there is no need for ADMM, ADMM can however provide significant speedup and memory savings in case of diffuse basis sets. If it is a GW bandgap calculations, RI_SIGMA_X can also be used.

KEYWORD.NAME: PRINT_DGEMM_INFO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print details about all DGEMM calls.

SECTION.NAME: HF
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up the Hartree-Fock parameters if requested

KEYWORD.NAME: FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The fraction of Hartree-Fock to add to the total energy. 1.0 implies standard Hartree-Fock if used with XC_FUNCTIONAL NONE. NOTE: In a mixed potential calculation this should be set to 1.0, otherwise all parts are multiplied with this factor.

KEYWORD.NAME: TREAT_LSD_IN_CORE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines how spin densities are taken into account. If true, the beta spin density is included via a second in core call. If false, alpha and beta spins are done in one shot

KEYWORD.NAME: PW_HFX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Compute the Hartree-Fock energy also in the plane wave basis. The value is ignored, and intended for debugging only.

KEYWORD.NAME: PW_HFX_BLOCKSIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Improve the performance of pw_hfx at the cost of some additional memory by storing the realspace representation of PW_HFX_BLOCKSIZE states.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing basic info about hf method

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the near field part of the electronic repulsion integrals using the Schwarz inequality for the given threshold.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCHWARZ_FORCES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the near field part of the electronic repulsion integrals using the Schwarz inequality for the given threshold. This will be approximately the accuracy of the forces, and should normally be similar to EPS_SCF

KEYWORD.NAME: SCREEN_P_FORCES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screens the electronic repulsion integrals for the forces using the density matrix. This results in a significant speedup for large systems, but might require a somewhat tigher EPS_SCHWARZ_FORCES.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCREEN_ON_INITIAL_P
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Screen on an initial density matrix. For the first MD step this matrix must be provided by a Restart File.

KEYWORD.NAME: P_SCREEN_CORRECTION_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Recalculates integrals on the fly if the actual density matrix is larger by a given factor than the initial one. If the factor is set to 0.0_dp, this feature is disabled.

ITEM.NAME: MIX_LG

ITEM.NAME: IDENTITY

KEYWORD.NAME: RANDOMIZE
