KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How the preconditioner is applied to the residual.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_GAP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Should be an estimate for the energy gap [a.u.] (HOMO-LUMO) and is used in preconditioning, especially effective with the FULL_ALL preconditioner, in which case it should be an underestimate of the gap (can be a small number, e.g. 0.002). FULL_SINGLE_INVERSE takes it as lower bound (values below 0.05 can cause stability issues). In general, higher values will tame the preconditioner in case of poor initial guesses. A negative value will leave the choice to CP2K depending on type of preconditioner.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_TAYLOR
EPSTAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Target accuracy of the taylor expansion for the matrix functions, should normally be kept as is.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_TAYLOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum order of the Taylor expansion before diagonalisation is preferred, for large parallel runs a slightly higher order could sometimes result in a small speedup.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROTATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Introduce additional variables so that rotations of the occupied subspace are allowed as well, only needed for cases where the energy is not invariant under a rotation of the occupied subspace such as non-singlet restricted calculations or fractional occupations.

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Optimize orbital energies for use in Fermi-Dirac smearing (requires ROTATION and FD smearing to be active).

KEYWORD.NAME: OCCUPATION_PRECONDITIONER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preconditioner with the occupation numbers (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Add a non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: NONDIAG_ENERGY_STRENGTH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The prefactor for the non-diagonal energy penalty (FD smearing)

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_JACOBI
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Below this threshold value for the SCF convergence the pseudo-diagonalization method using Jacobi rotations is activated. This method is much faster than a real diagonalization and it is even speeding up while achieving full convergence. However, it needs a pre-converged wavefunction obtained by at least one real diagonalization which is further optimized while keeping the original eigenvalue spectrum. The MO eigenvalues are NOT updated. The method might be useful to speed up calculations for large systems e.g. using a semi-empirical method.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Required accuracy in iterative diagonalization as compared to current SCF convergence

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do nothing, useful only with the none type

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Newton's method with backtracking line search to find the optimal step size. Only compatible with CDFT constraints. Potentially very expensive because each iteration performs a full SCF calculation.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of times the same point will be used in bisection, a small number guards against the effect of wrongly converged states.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The target gradient of the outer SCF variables. Notice that the EPS_SCF of the inner loop also determines the value that can be reached in the outer loop, typically EPS_SCF of the outer loop must be smaller than or equal to EPS_SCF of the inner loop.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIIS_BUFFER_LENGTH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of DIIS vectors used

KEYWORD.NAME: EXTRAPOLATION_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of past states used in the extrapolation of the variables during e.g. MD

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The maximum number of outer loops

KEYWORD.NAME: STEP_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The initial step_size used in the optimizer (currently steepest descent). Note that in cases where a sadle point is sought for (constrained DFT), this can be negative. For Newton and Broyden optimizers, use a value less/higher than the default 1.0 (in absolute value, the sign is not significant) to active an under/overrelaxed optimizer.

SECTION.NAME: CDFT_OPT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters controlling optimization methods that are compatible only with CDFT based constraints (i.e. CDFT SCF is active). Specifically, the control parameters for the Broyden and Newton optimizers are defined in this section.

KEYWORD.NAME: BROYDEN_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: BT1
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden's first method, also known as the good method. The initial Jacobian is built from MD history if available. Otherwise switches to SD for one SCF iteration until a Jacobian can be built from the SCF history.

ITEM.NAME: BT1_EXPLICIT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but computes the explicit Jacobian with finite differences. Requires a CDFT SCF procedure to be active.

ITEM.NAME: BT2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but uses Broyden's second method, also known as the bad method.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_EXPLICIT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1_EXPLICIT, but using Broyden's second method.

ITEM.NAME: BT1_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size (see optimizer NEWTON_LS).

ITEM.NAME: BT1_EXPLICIT_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT1_EXPLICIT, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT2, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

ITEM.NAME: BT2_EXPLICIT_LS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Same as BT2_EXPLICIT, but uses backtracking line search for optimizing the step size.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the Broyden optimizer variant to use.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: FD1
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order forward difference (one extra energy evaluation per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD1_BACKWARD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order backward difference (one extra energy evaluation per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Second order forward difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD2_BACKWARD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Second order backward difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

ITEM.NAME: FD1_CENTRAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: First order central difference (two extra energy evaluations per constraint).

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Finite difference method used to calculate the inverse Jacobian needed by some optimizers. Compatible only with CDFT constraints.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_STEP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Step size to use in the calculation of the inverse Jacobian with finite differences. Expects one value for all constraints, or one value per constraint.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_FREQ
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines parameters that control how often the explicit Jacobian is built, which is needed by some optimizers. Expects two values. The first value determines how many consecutive CDFT SCF iterations should skip a rebuild, whereas the latter how many MD steps. The values can be zero (meaning never rebuild) or positive. Both values cannot be zero.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restart the inverse Jacobian using the vector defined with keyword JACOBIAN_VECTOR.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBIAN_VECTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the inverse Jacobian matrix. Useful for restarting calculations. Expects n^2 values where n is the total number of constraints. The matrix should be given in row major order.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The maximum number of backtracking line search steps to perform.

KEYWORD.NAME: FACTOR_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Control parameter for backtracking line search. The step size is reduced by this factor on every line search iteration. Value must be between 0 and 1 (exclusive).

KEYWORD.NAME: CONTINUE_LS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Continue backtracking line search until MAX_LS steps are reached or the norm of the CDFT gradient no longer decreases. Default (false) behavior exits the line search procedure on the first step that the gradient decreases.

SECTION.NAME: SMEAR
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define the smearing of the MO occupation numbers

ITEM.NAME: FERMI_DIRAC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Fermi-Dirac distribution defined by the keyword ELECTRONIC_TEMPERATURE

ITEM.NAME: ENERGY_WINDOW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Energy window defined by the keyword WINDOW_SIZE

ITEM.NAME: LIST
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use a fixed list of occupations

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A list of fractional occupations to use. Must match the number of states and sum up to the correct number of electrons

KEYWORD.NAME: ELECTRONIC_TEMPERATURE
ELEC_TEMP
TELEC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Electronic temperature in the case of Fermi-Dirac smearing

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FERMI_DIRAC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Accuracy checks on occupation numbers use this as a tolerance

KEYWORD.NAME: WINDOW_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Size of the energy window centred at the Fermi level

KEYWORD.NAME: FIXED_MAGNETIC_MOMENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Imposed difference between the numbers of electrons of spin up and spin down: m = n(up) - n(down). A negative value (default) allows for a change of the magnetic moment. -1 specifically keeps an integer number of spin up and spin down electrons.

SECTION.NAME: MIXING
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define type and parameters for mixing procedures to be applied to the density matrix. Normally, only one type of mixing method should be accepted. The mixing procedures activated by this section are only active for diagonalization methods and linear scaling SCF, i.e. not with minimization methods based on OT.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the mixing procedure

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No mixing is applied

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT_P_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Direct mixing of new and old density matrices

ITEM.NAME: KERKER_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mixing of the potential in reciprocal space using the Kerker damping

ITEM.NAME: PULAY_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Pulay mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing

ITEM.NAME: BROYDEN_MIXING_NEW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Broyden mixing second version

ITEM.NAME: MULTISECANT_MIXING
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Multisecant scheme for mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be included

KEYWORD.NAME: BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Denominator parameter in Kerker damping introduced to suppress charge sloshing: rho_mix(g) = rho_in(g) + alpha*g^2/(g^2 + beta^2)*(rho_out(g)-rho_in(g))

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of new density to be added to the Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: PULAY_BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of residual contribution to be added to Pulay expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: NMIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Minimal number of density mixing (should be greater than 0), before starting DIIS

KEYWORD.NAME: NBUFFER
NPULAY
NBROYDEN
NMULTISECANT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of previous steps stored for the actual mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: BROY_W0
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: w0 parameter used in Broyden mixing

KEYWORD.NAME: REGULARIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Regularization parameter to stabilize the inversion of the residual matrix {Yn^t Yn} in the multisecant mixing scheme (noise)

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_STEP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Upper bound for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: R_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Control factor for the magnitude of the unpredicted step size in the update by the multisecant mixing scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: NSKIP
NSKIP_MIXING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of initial iteration for which the mixing is skipped

KEYWORD.NAME: N_SIMPLE_MIX
NSIMPLEMIX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of kerker damping iterations before starting other mixing procedures

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_GVEC_EXP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restricts the G-space mixing to lower part of G-vector spectrum, up to a G0, by assigning the exponent of the Gaussian that can be represented by vectors smaller than G0 within a certain accuracy.

KEYWORD.NAME: GMIX_P
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Activate the mixing of the density matrix, using the same mixing coefficient applied for the g-space mixing.

SECTION.NAME: MOM
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define type and parameters for the maximum overlap method (MOM) to determine orbital occupancies. The MOM procedures activated by this section are only active for diagonalization methods, i.e. not with minimization methods based on OT. Incompatible with core-level excitation spectra (XAS).

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the MOM procedure

KEYWORD.NAME: MOM_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: MOM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Originally proposed MOM protocol which uses molecular orbitals from the previous SCF cycle as reference

ITEM.NAME: IMOM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Initial-MOM which uses molecular orbitals of the initial guess as reference

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Revision of the maximum overlap method to be used

KEYWORD.NAME: START_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: SCF iteration cycle to start the MOM procedure. Could be used for ground state calculations only in order to stabilise oscillating SCF iterations

ITEM.NAME: NORM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The one which ignores the phase of molecular orbitals: proj_j = \sqrt(\sum_i overlap(i, j)^2)

ITEM.NAME: SUM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The one proposed in the original paper: proj_j = |\sum_i overlap(i, j)|

SECTION.NAME: PRINT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Printing of information during the SCF.

KEYWORD.NAME: DM_RESTART_WRITE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the density matrix into a binary file at the end of the SCF.

SECTION.NAME: RESTART
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the dumping of the MO restart file during SCF. By default keeps a short history of three restarts. See also RESTART_HISTORY

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: BACKUP_COPIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the maximum number of backup copies.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: JUST_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for an ENERGY/ENERGY_FORCE calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: POWELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for POWELL based optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: QS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the SCF steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: XAS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) SCF steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: MD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the MD steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: PINT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Path integral md steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: METADYNAMICS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the METADYNAMICS steps (number of hills added).

KEYWORD.NAME: GEO_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Geometry optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROT_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Rotational optimization steps in the Dimer calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: CELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Cell optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: BAND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the BAND calculation steps

KEYWORD.NAME: EP_LIN_SOLVER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Energy Perturbation (EP) linear solver

KEYWORD.NAME: SPLINE_FIND_COEFFS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the solution of the coefficients of the splines

KEYWORD.NAME: REPLICA_EVAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the evaluation of the Replica Environment

KEYWORD.NAME: BSSE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Basis Set Superposition Error (BSSE) calculation

KEYWORD.NAME: SHELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Shell-Core distances optimization steps

KEYWORD.NAME: TDDFT_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory SCF steps.

Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Rotational optimization steps in the Dimer calculation.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Cell optimization steps.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the BAND calculation steps

KEYWORD.NAME: SPLINE_FIND_COEFFS

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the evaluation of the Replica Environment

KEYWORD.NAME: BSSE

SECTION.NAME: MO_MAGNITUDE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Prints the min/max eigenvalues of the overlap of the MOs without S (CT C).

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: LOCALIZE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Use one of the available methods to define the localization and possibly to optimize it to a minimum or a maximum.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: controls the activation of the MOS localization procedure

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of iterations used for localization methods

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_CRAZY_ANGLE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Largest allowed angle for the crazy rotations algorithm (smaller is slower but more stable).

KEYWORD.NAME: CRAZY_USE_DIAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use diagonalization (slow) or pade based calculation of matrix exponentials.

KEYWORD.NAME: USE_HISTORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Generate an improved initial guess based on a history of results, which is useful during MD. Will only work if the number of states to be localized remains constant.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_OCCUPATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance in the occupation number to select only fully occupied orbitals for the rotation

KEYWORD.NAME: OUT_ITER_EACH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Every how many iterations of the localization algorithm (Jacobi) the tolerance value is printed out

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_LOCALIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance used in the convergence criterion of the localization methods.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_OR_MAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Requires the maximization of the spread of the wfn

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No localization is applied

ITEM.NAME: JACOBI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using 2 x 2 rotations of the orbitals, slow but robust

ITEM.NAME: CRAZY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: A new fast method is applied, might be slightly less robust than jacobi, but usually much faster

ITEM.NAME: GAPO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Gradient ascent for partially occupied wannier functions

ITEM.NAME: L1SD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Steepest descent minimization of an approximate l1 norm

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using a direct minimisation approacha

ITEM.NAME: SCDM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use QR factorization

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial guess for coefficients if METHOD GAPO is used

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS_SPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Orbital space from which initial guess for coefficients is determined if METHOD GAPO and CPO_GUESS ATOMIC are employed

KEYWORD.NAME: CG_PO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use conjugate gradient in conjunction with METHOD GAPO. If FALSE, steepest descent is used instead.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_FALLBACK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method in case no convergence was achieved by using the crazy rotations method.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_REFINEMENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method to refine the localisation obtained by SCDM

KEYWORD.NAME: RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restart the localization from a set of orbitals read from a localization restart file.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCHOMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for occupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCMIXD_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for MIXED states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCLUMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for unoccupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: OPERATOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of opertator which defines the spread functional

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the occupied wfn to be localized This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST_UNOCCUPIED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the unoccupied states to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present if unoccupied states should be localized. This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: NEXTRA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of orbitals above fully occupied MOs to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present for STATES MIXED option. Otherwise, only the fully occupied MOs are localized.

KEYWORD.NAME: STATES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which states to localize, LUMO up to now only available in GPW

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_RANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Select the orbitals to be localized within the given energy range. This type of selection cannot be added on top of the selection through a LIST. It reads to reals that are lower and higher boundaries of the energy range.

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write only the coordinates X,Y,Z without element symbols to a formatted file

ITEM.NAME: DCD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write the coordinates (no element labels) and the cell information to a binary file

ITEM.NAME: DCD_ALIGNED_CELL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Like DCD, but the dumped coordinates refer to an aligned cell following the common convention: the cell vector **a** is aligned with the *x* axis and the cell vector **b** lies in the *xy* plane. This allows the reconstruction of scaled coordinates from the DCD data only.

ITEM.NAME: PDB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write the atomic information in PDB format to a formatted file

ITEM.NAME: XMOL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mostly known as XYZ format, provides in a formatted file: element_symbol X Y Z

ITEM.NAME: XYZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Alias name for XMOL

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the format of the output file when IONS+CENTERS is enabled.

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE_BETA

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE_EXTENDED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the MM charges to the very last field of the PDB file (starting from column 81)

KEYWORD.NAME: PRINT_ATOM_KIND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the atom kind given in the subsys section instead of the element symbol. Only valid for the XMOL format.

KEYWORD.NAME: MARK_STATES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Can be used to mark given molecular states. Sets a mark to both, occupied and unoccupied states. Occupied states are counted beginning with HOMO=1, unoccupied states are counted beginning with LUMO=1, This is only meaningful in combination with WFN_MIX. First integer specifies the molecule, second integer specifies the state.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of local PDOS, projected on subsets of atoms given through lists

KEYWORD.NAME: COMPONENTS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print out pdos distinguishing all angular momentum components.

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies a list of indexes of atoms where to project the DOS

SECTION.NAME: R_LDOS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of local PDOS, projected on 3D volume in real space, the volume is defined in terms of position with respect to atoms in the lists

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies a list of indexes of atoms used to define the real space volume

KEYWORD.NAME: XRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction x: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: YRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction y: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: ZRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction z: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: ERANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: only project states with the eigenvalues in the given interval. Default is all states.

SECTION.NAME: RESTART
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the dumping of MO restart file during the SCF. of a Core-Level-Spectroscopy calculation. For each new excited atom, one different restart file is dumped. These restart files should be employed only to restart the same type of CLS calculation, i.e. with the same core potential.

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: append the cube files when they already exist

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The energy range in eV for which excitations are considered. Only excitated states within the range of: first excitation energy + ENERGY_RANGE are kept. If ENERGY_RANGE and N_EXCITED are specified, the former has priority. Negative values are ignored and N_EXCITED takes over.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Defines how the kernel is built in terms of functionals.

KEYWORD.NAME: RI_REGION
RI_RADIUS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The region defined by a sphere of the given radius around the excited atom defining which RI_XAS basis elements are considered for the RI projection of the density. Each basis element which center is in this region is taken. The density for a given excited atom is expressed as : sum_ijkl P_ij (ijk) S_kl^-1 xi_l, where P_ij is the density matrix, i,j span the orbital basis and k,l the RI_XAS basis in the region. The larger the radius, the more basis functions to expand the density. However, it is assumed that it is a small number and the code does not scale well as the number of RI basis elements gets too large. Expressed in Angstrom. If the radius is set to 0.0, only the RI basis elements centered on the excited atom are used.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A threshold to determine which primitive 3-center integrals are kept for contraction, as the latter operation can be expensive (especially for large basis sets ). If |(ab|c)| < EPS_SCREENNING, it is discarded.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCALE

SECTION.NAME: RI_METRIC
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This subsection allows for the definition of an exchange RI metric that is different from the main exchange potential. By default (i.e. if this subsection is ignored), the exchange kernel is computed in the V approximation: (ab|ij) = (ab|P) V^-1 (Q|ij), where V = (P|Q). With a RI metric, we have a 2 step RI involving the metric potential for the 3-center integrals: (ab|ij) = (ab!P) (P!Q)^-1 (Q|R) (R!S)^-1 (S!ij), where | stands for the exchange potential and ! for the metric potential. This allows for drastic screening of the 3-center integrals by selecting shorter range metric.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Enables the use of a RI metric.

SECTION.NAME: LOCALIZE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Use one of the available methods to define the localization and possibly to optimize it to a minimum or a maximum.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: controls the activation of the MOS localization procedure

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of iterations used for localization methods

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_CRAZY_ANGLE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Largest allowed angle for the crazy rotations algorithm (smaller is slower but more stable).

KEYWORD.NAME: CRAZY_USE_DIAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use diagonalization (slow) or pade based calculation of matrix exponentials.

KEYWORD.NAME: USE_HISTORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Generate an improved initial guess based on a history of results, which is useful during MD. Will only work if the number of states to be localized remains constant.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_OCCUPATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance in the occupation number to select only fully occupied orbitals for the rotation

KEYWORD.NAME: OUT_ITER_EACH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Every how many iterations of the localization algorithm (Jacobi) the tolerance value is printed out

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_LOCALIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance used in the convergence criterion of the localization methods.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_OR_MAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Requires the maximization of the spread of the wfn

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No localization is applied

ITEM.NAME: JACOBI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using 2 x 2 rotations of the orbitals, slow but robust

ITEM.NAME: CRAZY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: A new fast method is applied, might be slightly less robust than jacobi, but usually much faster

ITEM.NAME: GAPO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Gradient ascent for partially occupied wannier functions

ITEM.NAME: L1SD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Steepest descent minimization of an approximate l1 norm

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using a direct minimisation approacha

ITEM.NAME: SCDM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use QR factorization

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial guess for coefficients if METHOD GAPO is used

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS_SPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Orbital space from which initial guess for coefficients is determined if METHOD GAPO and CPO_GUESS ATOMIC are employed

KEYWORD.NAME: CG_PO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use conjugate gradient in conjunction with METHOD GAPO. If FALSE, steepest descent is used instead.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_FALLBACK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method in case no convergence was achieved by using the crazy rotations method.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_REFINEMENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method to refine the localisation obtained by SCDM

KEYWORD.NAME: RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restart the localization from a set of orbitals read from a localization restart file.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCHOMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for occupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCMIXD_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for MIXED states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCLUMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for unoccupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: OPERATOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of opertator which defines the spread functional

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the occupied wfn to be localized This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST_UNOCCUPIED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the unoccupied states to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present if unoccupied states should be localized. This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: NEXTRA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of orbitals above fully occupied MOs to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present for STATES MIXED option. Otherwise, only the fully occupied MOs are localized.

KEYWORD.NAME: STATES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which states to localize, LUMO up to now only available in GPW

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_RANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Select the orbitals to be localized within the given energy range. This type of selection cannot be added on top of the selection through a LIST. It reads to reals that are lower and higher boundaries of the energy range.

SECTION.NAME: PRINT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Collects all printing options related to the Wannier centers and properties computed with Wannier centers.

SECTION.NAME: PROGRAM_RUN_INFO
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing basic info about the method

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: FORMAT

ITEM.NAME: ATOMIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write only the coordinates X,Y,Z without element symbols to a formatted file

ITEM.NAME: DCD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write the coordinates (no element labels) and the cell information to a binary file

ITEM.NAME: DCD_ALIGNED_CELL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Like DCD, but the dumped coordinates refer to an aligned cell following the common convention: the cell vector **a** is aligned with the *x* axis and the cell vector **b** lies in the *xy* plane. This allows the reconstruction of scaled coordinates from the DCD data only.

ITEM.NAME: PDB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Write the atomic information in PDB format to a formatted file

ITEM.NAME: XMOL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mostly known as XYZ format, provides in a formatted file: element_symbol X Y Z

ITEM.NAME: XYZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Alias name for XMOL

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the format of the output file when IONS+CENTERS is enabled.

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE_OCCUP
CHARGE_O
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the MM charges to the OCCUP field of the PDB file

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE_BETA
CHARGE_B
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the MM charges to the BETA field of the PDB file

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE_EXTENDED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the MM charges to the very last field of the PDB file (starting from column 81)

KEYWORD.NAME: PRINT_ATOM_KIND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Write the atom kind given in the subsys section instead of the element symbol. Only valid for the XMOL format.

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Berry phase formula (PERIODIC=T) or simple operator (PERIODIC=F). The latter normally requires that the CELL is periodic NONE.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFERENCE
REF

ITEM.NAME: COM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Mass

ITEM.NAME: COAC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Atomic Charges

ITEM.NAME: USER_DEFINED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use User Defined Point (Keyword:REF_POINT)

ITEM.NAME: ZERO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Origin of Coordinate System

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Define the reference point for the calculation of the electrostatic moment.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFERENCE_POINT
REF_POINT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fixed reference point for the calculations of the electrostatic moment.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: REAL_TIME_PROPAGATION
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters needed to set up the real time propagation for the electron dynamics. This currently works only in the NVE ensemble.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximal number of iterations for the self consistent propagator loop.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Convergence criterion for the self consistent propagator loop.

KEYWORD.NAME: ASPC_ORDER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Speciefies how many steps will be used for extrapolation. One will be always used which is means X(t+dt)=X(t)

KEYWORD.NAME: MAT_EXP

ITEM.NAME: TAYLOR
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: exponential is evaluated using scaling and squaring in combination with a taylor expansion of the exponential.

ITEM.NAME: PADE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: uses scaling and squaring together with the pade approximation

ITEM.NAME: ARNOLDI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: uses arnoldi subspace algorithm to compute exp(H)*MO directly, can't be used in combination with Crank Nicholson or density propagation

ITEM.NAME: BCH
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Uses a Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion to propagate the density matrix, only works for density propagation

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which method should be used to calculate the exponential in the propagator. It is recommended to use BCH when employing density_propagation and ARNOLDI otherwise.

KEYWORD.NAME: DENSITY_PROPAGATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The density matrix is propagated instead of the molecular orbitals. This can allow a linear scaling simulation. The density matrix is filtered with the threshold based on the EPS_FILTER keyword from the LS_SCF section

KEYWORD.NAME: SC_CHECK_START
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Speciefies how many iteration steps will be done without a check for self consistency. Can save some time in big calculations.

KEYWORD.NAME: EXP_ACCURACY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Accuracy for the taylor and pade approximation. This is only an upper bound bound since the norm used for the guess is an upper bound for the needed one.

KEYWORD.NAME: PROPAGATOR

ITEM.NAME: ETRS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: enforced time reversible symmetry

ITEM.NAME: CN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Crank Nicholson propagator

ITEM.NAME: EM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Exponential midpoint propagator

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which propagator should be used for the orbitals

KEYWORD.NAME: INITIAL_WFN

ITEM.NAME: SCF_WFN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: An SCF run is performed to get the initial state.

ITEM.NAME: RESTART_WFN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: A wavefunction from a previous SCF is propagated. Especially useful, if electronic constraints or restraints are used in the previous calculation, since these do not work in the rtp scheme.

ITEM.NAME: RT_RESTART
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: use the wavefunction of a real time propagation/ehrenfest run

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Controls the initial WFN used for propagation. Note that some energy contributions may not be initialized in the restart cases, for instance electronic entropy energy in the case of smearing.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPLY_WFN_MIX_INIT_RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If set to True and in the case of INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN, call the DFT%PRINT%WFN_MIX section to mix the read initial wfn. The starting wave-function of the RTP will be the mixed one. Setting this to True without a defined WFN_MIX section will not do anything as defining a WFN_MIX section without this keyword for RTP run with INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN. Note that if INITIAL_WFN=SCF_WFN, this keyword is not needed to apply the mixing defined in the WFN_MIX section. Default is False.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPLY_DELTA_PULSE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Applies a delta kick to the initial wfn (only RTP for now - the EMD case is not yet implemented). Only work for INITIAL_WFN=SCF_WFN

KEYWORD.NAME: APPLY_DELTA_PULSE_MAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Applies a magnetic delta kick to the initial wfn (only RTP for now - the EMD case is not yet implemented). Only work for INITIAL_WFN=SCF_WFN

KEYWORD.NAME: VELOCITY_GAUGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Perform propagation in the velocity gauge using the explicit vector potential only a constant vector potential as of now (corresonding to a delta-pulse). uses DELTA_PULSE_SCALE and DELTA_PULSE_DIRECTION to define the vector potential

KEYWORD.NAME: GAUGE_ORIG

ITEM.NAME: COM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Mass

ITEM.NAME: COAC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Atomic Charges

ITEM.NAME: USER_DEFINED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use User Defined Point (Keyword:REF_POINT)

ITEM.NAME: ZERO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Origin of Coordinate System

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Define gauge origin for magnetic perturbation

KEYWORD.NAME: GAUGE_ORIG_MANUAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Manually defined gauge origin for magnetic perturbation [in Bohr!]

KEYWORD.NAME: VG_COM_NL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: apply gauge transformed non-local potential term only affects VELOCITY_GAUGE=.TRUE.

KEYWORD.NAME: COM_NL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Include non-local commutator for periodic delta pulse. only affects PERIODIC=.TRUE.

KEYWORD.NAME: LEN_REP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use length representation delta pulse (in conjunction with PERIODIC T). This corresponds to a 1st order perturbation in the length gauge. Note that this is NOT compatible with a periodic calculation! Uses the reference point defined in DFT%PRINT%MOMENTS

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Apply a delta-kick that is compatible with periodic boundary conditions for any value of DELTA_PULSE_SCALE. Uses perturbation theory for the preparation of the initial wfn with the velocity operator as perturbation. If LEN_REP is .FALSE. this corresponds to a first order velocity gauge. Note that the pulse is only applied when INITIAL_WFN is set to SCF_WFN, and not for restarts (RT_RESTART).

KEYWORD.NAME: DELTA_PULSE_DIRECTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Direction of the applied electric field. The k vector is given as 2*Pi*[i,j,k]*inv(h_mat), which for PERIODIC .FALSE. yields exp(ikr) periodic with the unit cell, only if DELTA_PULSE_SCALE is set to unity. For an orthorhombic cell [1,0,0] yields [2*Pi/L_x,0,0]. For small cells, this results in a very large kick.

KEYWORD.NAME: DELTA_PULSE_SCALE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scale the k vector, which for PERIODIC .FALSE. results in exp(ikr) no longer being periodic with the unit cell. The norm of k is the strength of the applied electric field in atomic units.

KEYWORD.NAME: HFX_BALANCE_IN_CORE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If HFX is used, this keyword forces a redistribution/recalculation of the integrals, balanced with respect to the in core steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: MCWEENY_MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines the maximum amount of McWeeny steps used after each converged step in density propagation

KEYWORD.NAME: ACCURACY_REFINEMENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If using density propagation some parts should be calculated with a higher accuracy than the rest to reduce numerical noise. This factor determines by how much the filtering threshold is reduced for these calculations.

KEYWORD.NAME: MCWEENY_EPS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold after which McWeeny is terminated

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: PROJECTION_MO
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Projects the Time Dependent (TD) MO coefficients to reference ones. You can define several sections like this to project the TD-MOs on different reference MOs. Note that each section projects from one spin of the TD MOs (TD_MO_INDEX) to one spin of the reference MOs (REF_MO_INDEX).

KEYWORD.NAME: PROPAGATE_REF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: In the case of Ehrenfest dynamics, the atomic basis set is evolving with time. The reference MO can either be understood as a spatial-dependent wave-function which is time-independent or to be 'attached' with respect to the nuclei position, and thus evolve in space as the nuclei move. For the first case, set this variable to TRUE. Note that in this case, you shall have enough atomic orbital across the whole space to describe this MO as the nuclei will move and may leave the space where the MO is defined. For the second case, set to FALSE (default). Note that in this case, if the nuclei undergo dramatic changes (dissociation for instance) then this definition may make no longer sense.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFERENCE_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: SCF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The reference MO is from an SCF calculation.

ITEM.NAME: XAS_TDP
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The reference MO is from an XAS_TDP analysis.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of the reference MO file provided in REF_MO_FILE_NAME.

KEYWORD.NAME: REF_MO_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Name of the wavefunction file to read the reference MO from. For instance, a restart wfn file from SCF calculation or an excited state from XAS_TDP calculation. If no file is specified, the default is to use DFT%WFN_RESTART_FILE_NAME. Currently, a RTP restart file (.rtpwfn) cannot be used as reference. Currently, this file SHALL have the same number of spin as the propagated one (eventhough you use only the first spin from this reference).

KEYWORD.NAME: REF_MO_INDEX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the reference MO read from the .wfn reference file (see REF_MO_FILE_NAME). Use this keyword if REFERENCE_TYPE=SCF. Set to -1 to project on all the MO available. One file will be generated per index defined.

KEYWORD.NAME: REF_MO_SPIN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Spin of the reference MOs to consider. 1 for ALPHA and 2 for BETA spin respectively. If the reference MO is spin independent this key is not used.

KEYWORD.NAME: SUM_ON_ALL_REF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Set to .TRUE. in order to sum all the projections done over the required MO_REF_INDEX for each TD MOs. Only one file will be generated containing the results for every MO_TD_INDEX.

KEYWORD.NAME: TD_MO_INDEX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the time dependent MOs to project on the reference MOs. Set to -1 to project on all the TD MOs.

KEYWORD.NAME: TD_MO_SPIN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Spin of the TD MOs to consider. 1 for ALPHA spin, 2 for BETA spin. If the TD calculation is spin independent this key is not used.

KEYWORD.NAME: SUM_ON_ALL_TD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Set to .TRUE. in order to sum the projection done over all on TD MOs on the required MO_REF_INDEX. One file per MO_REF_INDEX will be generated. Combining SUM_ON_ALL_TD and SUM_ON_ALL_REF lead to one file one projection: the population of all the defined TD_MO_INDEX over the reference MO_REF_INDEX per time step required.

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). SECTION.NAME: MO
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of the molecular orbital (MO) information. The requested MO information is printed for all occupied MOs by default. Use the MO_INDEX_RANGE keyword to restrict the number of the MOs or to print the MO information for unoccupied MOs. With diagonalization, additional MOs have to be made available for printout using the ADDED_MOS keyword in the SCF section. With OT, it is sufficient to specify the desired MO_INDEX_RANGE. The OT eigensolver can be controlled with the EPS_LUMO and MAX_ITER_LUMO keywords in the SCF section.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: NLUMO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the printkey is activated controls the number of additional lumos that are computed to be able to reproduce STM images obtained from positive bias (imaging unoccupied states)

KEYWORD.NAME: BIAS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Bias energy for scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) image generation. Orbital densities are summed according to the bias energy. For negative values, states in the range ]EF+bias,EF] are summed, While positive values sum states in the range [EF,EF+bias[. If positive biases are used, sufficiently many unoccupied stated (see ADDED_MOS and NLUMO ) should be computed.

KEYWORD.NAME: TH_TORB

ITEM.NAME: S
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: s orbital

ITEM.NAME: PX
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: px orbital

ITEM.NAME: PY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: py orbital

ITEM.NAME: PZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: pz orbital

ITEM.NAME: DXY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: dxy orbital

ITEM.NAME: DYZ
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: dyz orbital

ITEM.NAME: DZX
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: dzx orbital

ITEM.NAME: DX2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: x^2 orbital

ITEM.NAME: DY2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: y^2 orbital

ITEM.NAME: DZ2
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: z^2 orbital

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tip orbital symmetry in Tersoff-Hamann approximation to compute STM images

KEYWORD.NAME: REF_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: By default the reference energy is the Fermi energy. In order to compare with STS experiments, where specific energy ranges are addressed, here one can set a different reference energy. The energy range is anyway controlled by the BIAS

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: append the cube files when they already exist

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: WFN_MIX
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: A section that allows manipulation of the MO coeffs, e.g. for changing a ground state into an excited state. Starting from a copy of the original MOs, changes can be made by adding linear combinations of HOMO/LUMO of the original MOs to the result MOs. This method is called after an SCF optimization or before an RTP run if INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN. Note that if called after an SCF optimization, a restart file with the mixed MOs is saved. This is not the case for an RTP with INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN.

KEYWORD.NAME: OVERWRITE_MOS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If set to True, the active molecular orbitals in memory will be replaced by the mixed wfn at the end of the wfn mixing procedure. For instance, you can then use this new set of MOs to perform RTP or EMD directly. Not that in the case of an RTP run with INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN, this keyword is not used: the mixed wfn is used to start the time-dependent run. Default value is False.

SECTION.NAME: UPDATE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: update a result MO with with a linear combination of of original MOs. This section can be repeated to build arbitrary linear combinations using repeatedly y=a*y+b*x.

KEYWORD.NAME: RESULT_MO_INDEX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Index of the MO (y) to be modified. Counting down in energy: set to 1 for the HOMO, to 3 for the HOMO-3.

KEYWORD.NAME: RESULT_MARKED_STATE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the MO according to the marks set in MOLECULAR_STATES. The value corresponds to the repetition of MARK_STATES in MOLECULAR_STATES

KEYWORD.NAME: RESULT_SPIN_INDEX

ITEM.NAME: ALPHA
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Majority spin

ITEM.NAME: BETA
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Minority spin

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Spin of the MO (y) to be modified.

KEYWORD.NAME: RESULT_SCALE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor of the result variable (a).

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_MO_INDEX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Index of the original MO (x). If ORIG_TYPE is OCCUPIED, it counts down in energy: set to 1 to point to the HOMO and to 3 for the HOMO-3. If ORIG_TYPE is VIRTUAL, it counts up in energy: set to 1 to point to the LUMO and to 3 for the LUMO+3. If ORIG_TYPE is EXTERNAL, it counts down in energy for the external set of MOs: set to 1 to point to the HOMO and to 3 for the HOMO-3. Do not set to zero or negative values.

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_MARKED_STATE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the MO according to the marks set in MOLECULAR_STATES. The value corresponds to the repetition of MARK_STATES in MOLECULAR_STATES

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_SPIN_INDEX

ITEM.NAME: ALPHA
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Majority spin

ITEM.NAME: BETA
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Minority spin

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Spin of the MO (x) to be modified.

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_SCALE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Scaling factor of the result variable (b).

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: OCCUPIED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The original MO is in the MOs matrix itself.

ITEM.NAME: VIRTUAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The original MO is not in the MOs matrix but in the 'unoccupied' one. The SCF cycle shall provide it.

ITEM.NAME: EXTERNAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: The orginal MO is from an external .wfn file. Use the keyword ORIG_EXT_FILE_NAME to define its name.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of the orgine MO. Note that using VIRTUAL along with an RTP run with INITIAL_WFN=RESTART_WFN will probably crash since no virtual state will be available.

KEYWORD.NAME: ORIG_EXT_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Name of the wavefunction file to read the original MO from. For instance, a restart wfn file from SCF calculation or an excited state from XAS_TDP calculation. If no file is specified, the run will crash. Currently, a RTP restart file (.rtpwfn) cannot be used as reference. Currently, this file SHALL have the basis set, number of MO and the same number of spin as the one from the SCF cycle.

KEYWORD.NAME: TOTAL_DENSITY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print the total electronic density in the case of a GAPW run. This keyword has only an effect, if PAW atoms are present. The default is to print only the soft part of the electronic density and to ignore the hard part. NOTE: The total density in real space might exhibit unphysical features like spikes due to the finite and thus truncated g vector expansion

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND

KEYWORD.NAME: XRD_INTERFACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: It activates the print out of exponents and coefficients for the Gaussian expansion of the core densities, based on atom calculations for each kind. The resulting core dansities are needed to compute the form factors. If GAPW the local densities are also given in terms of a Gaussian expansion, by fitting the difference between local-fhard and local-soft density for each atom. In this case the keyword TOTAL_DENSITY is set to FALSE

KEYWORD.NAME: NGAUSS

KEYWORD.NAME: PARAMETER_KEY

A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Appends frames to already existing .voronoi file.

KEYWORD.NAME: SANITY_CHECK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Performs a sanity check before each Voronoi integration, i.e., checks if every grid point is located in exactly one Voronoi cell.

KEYWORD.NAME: OVERWRITE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify this keyword to overwrite any existing "properties.emp" file if it already exists. By default, the data is appended to an existing .emp file.

KEYWORD.NAME: SKIP_FIRST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Skips the first step of a MD run (avoids duplicate step if restarted).

KEYWORD.NAME: VERBOSE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Switches on verbose screen output of the Voronoi integration.

KEYWORD.NAME: OUTPUT_EMP
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Writes the resulting electromagnetic moments to a binary file "properties.emp". The file name cannot be changed.

KEYWORD.NAME: OUTPUT_TEXT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Writes the resulting electromagnetic moments to text files (*.voronoi). The file name is specified via FILENAME.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFINEMENT_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets the refinement factor for the Voronoi integration.

KEYWORD.NAME: VORONOI_RADII

ITEM.NAME: UNITY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use unity radii (non-radical Voronoi tessellation)

ITEM.NAME: VDW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use VdW atom radii

ITEM.NAME: COVALENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use covalent atom radii

ITEM.NAME: USER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use user-specified atom radii

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which atomic radii to use for the radical Voronoi tessellation.

KEYWORD.NAME: USER_RADII
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines user atom radii for the radical Voronoi tessellation (one per atom).

KEYWORD.NAME: MOLECULAR_PROPERTIES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Calculation of molecular properties from Voronoi integration.

KEYWORD.NAME: MOLPROP_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Root of the file name where to print molecular properties. filename.molprop is used.

KEYWORD.NAME: JITTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Voronoi tessellation can have issues with highly symmetric structures. This keyword displaces all atoms pseudo-randomly by a tiny amount (see JITTER_AMPLITUDE) to break symmetry. The displacement is constant over time, so that no temporal noise is introduced. The displacement is not visible to other CP2k routines (FORCE_EVAL, output). It is only applied internally in the library for the Voronoi tessellation.

KEYWORD.NAME: JITTER_SEED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets the random seed for the jitter. The pseudo-random number generator is re-initialized for each Voronoi tessellation so that the jitter is constant over simulation time (no temporal noise).

KEYWORD.NAME: JITTER_AMPLITUDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets the maximum displacement amplitude for the jitter.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: JUST_ENERGY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for an ENERGY/ENERGY_FORCE calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: POWELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for POWELL based optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: QS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the SCF steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: XAS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) SCF steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: MD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the MD steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: PINT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Path integral md steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: METADYNAMICS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the METADYNAMICS steps (number of hills added).

KEYWORD.NAME: GEO_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Geometry optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: ROT_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Rotational optimization steps in the Dimer calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: CELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Cell optimization steps.

KEYWORD.NAME: BAND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the BAND calculation steps

KEYWORD.NAME: EP_LIN_SOLVER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Energy Perturbation (EP) linear solver

KEYWORD.NAME: SPLINE_FIND_COEFFS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the solution of the coefficients of the splines

KEYWORD.NAME: REPLICA_EVAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the evaluation of the Replica Environment

KEYWORD.NAME: BSSE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Basis Set Superposition Error (BSSE) calculation

KEYWORD.NAME: SHELL_OPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Shell-Core distances optimization steps

KEYWORD.NAME: TDDFT_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Iteration level for the Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory SCF steps.

SECTION.NAME: IMPLICIT_PSOLVER
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls printing of cube files for data from the implicit (generalized) Poisson solver.

SECTION.NAME: DIELECTRIC_CUBE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of a cube file with dielectric constant from the implicit (generalized) Poisson solver.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: append the cube files when they already exist

SECTION.NAME: DIRICHLET_BC_CUBE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of cube files with unit step functions (constraints) representing Dirichlet-type (boundary) regions defined in the implicit (generalized) Poisson solver section. The regions remain unchanged throughout the calculations. If the Dirichlet regions are relatively large and/or the number of partitions is quite high, in order to save memory, generate the cube files in early steps and perform the rest of the calculations with this keyword switched off.
