ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: append the cube files when they already exist

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print out pdos distinguishing all angular momentum components.

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies a list of indexes of atoms where to project the DOS

SECTION.NAME: R_LDOS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of local PDOS, projected on 3D volume in real space, the volume is defined in terms of position with respect to atoms in the lists

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies a list of indexes of atoms used to define the real space volume

KEYWORD.NAME: XRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction x: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: YRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction y: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: ZRANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: range of positions in Cartesian direction z: all grid points within this range from at least one atom of the list are considered

KEYWORD.NAME: ERANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: only project states with the eigenvalues in the given interval. Default is all states.

A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: COM_NL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Include non local commutator for velocity representations. Necessary for origin independent results.

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOM_LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the atoms minimal basis to be printed as cube files This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

SECTION.NAME: ENERGY_WINDOWS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Controls the printing of the DOS from the density matrix. This allows the calculation of the DOS even in density matrix based REAL_TIME_PROPAGATION and LS_SCF. However, it requires a cubically scaling diagonalization of the Hamiltonian. Hartree-Fock NYI, values will be wrong. Careful, the orbitals in rtp/emd are not actually eigenstates of the Hamiltonian. Assumes absence of spin polarization (so far).

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: THRESHOLD
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Threshold on the absolute value of the elements to be printed out. In CP2K all the elements in a (atomic) matrix block are considered non-zero, if the block contains at least one non-zero element.

KEYWORD.NAME: UPPER_TRIANGULAR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print only the upper triangular part of the matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: BINARY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to generate the file in a binary format.

KEYWORD.NAME: REAL_SPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print the overlap matrix in real-space instead of k-space..

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: STRIDE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The stride (X,Y,Z) used to write the cube file (larger values result in smaller cube files). You can provide 3 numbers (for X,Y,Z) or 1 number valid for all components.

KEYWORD.NAME: APPEND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Append the cube files when they already exist

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: SCCS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Define the parameters for self-consistent continuum solvation (SCCS) model

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the SCCS section

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Solvent specific tunable parameter for the calculation of the repulsion term $G^\text{rep} = \alpha S$ where $S$ is the (quantum) surface of the cavity

KEYWORD.NAME: BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Solvent specific tunable parameter for the calculation of the dispersion term $G^\text{dis} = \beta V$ where $V$ is the (quantum) volume of the cavity

KEYWORD.NAME: DELTA_RHO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Numerical increment for the calculation of the (quantum) surface of the solute cavity

KEYWORD.NAME: DERIVATIVE_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: FFT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Fast Fourier transformation

ITEM.NAME: CD3
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 3-point stencil central differences

ITEM.NAME: CD5
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 5-point stencil central differences

ITEM.NAME: CD7
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 7-point stencil central differences

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method for the calculation of the numerical derivatives on the real-space grids

KEYWORD.NAME: RELATIVE_PERMITTIVITY
DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT
EPSILON_RELATIVE
EPSILON_SOLVENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Relative permittivity (dielectric constant) of the solvent (medium)

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCCS
EPS_ITER
TAU_POL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance for the convergence of the polarisation density, i.e. requested accuracy for the SCCS iteration cycle

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SCF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The SCCS iteration cycle is activated only if the SCF iteration cycle is converged to this threshold value

KEYWORD.NAME: GAMMA
SURFACE_TENSION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Surface tension of the solvent used for the calculation of the cavitation term $G^\text{cav} = \gamma S$ where $S$ is the (quantum) surface of the cavity

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of SCCS iteration steps performed to converge within the given tolerance

KEYWORD.NAME: METHOD

ITEM.NAME: ANDREUSSI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Smoothing function proposed by Andreussi et al.

ITEM.NAME: FATTEBERT-GYGI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Smoothing function proposed by Fattebert and Gygi

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Method used for the smoothing of the dielectric function

KEYWORD.NAME: MIXING
ETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Mixing parameter (Hartree damping) employed during the iteration procedure

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Yukawa potential operator

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_INTEGRAL

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for the GPW approach to electron repulsion integrals.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_GRID
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines a threshold for the GPW based integration

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_FILTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines a threshold for the sparse matrix multiplications if METHOD GPW_HALF_TRANSFORM is used

KEYWORD.NAME: CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The cutoff of the finest grid level in the GPW integration.

KEYWORD.NAME: REL_CUTOFF
RELATIVE_CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Determines the grid at which a Gaussian is mapped.

KEYWORD.NAME: STORE_WFN
STORE_WAVEFUNCTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Store wavefunction in real space representation for integration.

KEYWORD.NAME: GROUP_SIZE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Sets the size of a subgroup for ERI calculation, each of which with a full set of work grids, arrays or orbitals depending on the method of grids (work grids, arrays, orbitals). Small numbers reduce communication but increase the memory demands. A negative number indicates all processes (default).

IOLEVEL

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Almost no output

ITEM.NAME: LOW
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Little output

ITEM.NAME: MEDIUM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Quite some output

ITEM.NAME: HIGH
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Lots of output

ITEM.NAME: DEBUG
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Everything is written out, useful for debugging purposes only

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How much output is written by the individual groups.

SECTION.NAME: LOCALIZE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Use one of the available methods to define the localization and possibly to optimize it to a minimum or a maximum.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: controls the activation of the MOS localization procedure

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of iterations used for localization methods

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_CRAZY_ANGLE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Largest allowed angle for the crazy rotations algorithm (smaller is slower but more stable).

KEYWORD.NAME: CRAZY_USE_DIAG
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use diagonalization (slow) or pade based calculation of matrix exponentials.

KEYWORD.NAME: USE_HISTORY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Generate an improved initial guess based on a history of results, which is useful during MD. Will only work if the number of states to be localized remains constant.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_OCCUPATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance in the occupation number to select only fully occupied orbitals for the rotation

KEYWORD.NAME: OUT_ITER_EACH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Every how many iterations of the localization algorithm (Jacobi) the tolerance value is printed out

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_LOCALIZATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Tolerance used in the convergence criterion of the localization methods.

KEYWORD.NAME: MIN_OR_MAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Requires the maximization of the spread of the wfn

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No localization is applied

ITEM.NAME: JACOBI
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using 2 x 2 rotations of the orbitals, slow but robust

ITEM.NAME: CRAZY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: A new fast method is applied, might be slightly less robust than jacobi, but usually much faster

ITEM.NAME: GAPO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Gradient ascent for partially occupied wannier functions

ITEM.NAME: L1SD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Steepest descent minimization of an approximate l1 norm

ITEM.NAME: DIRECT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using a direct minimisation approacha

ITEM.NAME: SCDM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use QR factorization

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Initial guess for coefficients if METHOD GAPO is used

KEYWORD.NAME: CPO_GUESS_SPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Orbital space from which initial guess for coefficients is determined if METHOD GAPO and CPO_GUESS ATOMIC are employed

KEYWORD.NAME: CG_PO
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use conjugate gradient in conjunction with METHOD GAPO. If FALSE, steepest descent is used instead.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_FALLBACK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method in case no convergence was achieved by using the crazy rotations method.

KEYWORD.NAME: JACOBI_REFINEMENT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Jacobi method to refine the localisation obtained by SCDM

KEYWORD.NAME: RESTART
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Restart the localization from a set of orbitals read from a localization restart file.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCHOMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for occupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCMIXD_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for MIXED states

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCLUMO_RESTART_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: File name where to read the MOS from which to restart the localization procedure for unoccupied states

KEYWORD.NAME: OPERATOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of opertator which defines the spread functional

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the occupied wfn to be localized This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: LIST_UNOCCUPIED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Indexes of the unoccupied states to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present if unoccupied states should be localized. This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

KEYWORD.NAME: NEXTRA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Number of orbitals above fully occupied MOs to be localized, up to now only valid in combination with GPW. This keyword has to be present for STATES MIXED option. Otherwise, only the fully occupied MOs are localized.

KEYWORD.NAME: STATES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Which states to localize, LUMO up to now only available in GPW

KEYWORD.NAME: ENERGY_RANGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Select the orbitals to be localized within the given energy range. This type of selection cannot be added on top of the selection through a LIST. It reads to reals that are lower and higher boundaries of the energy range.

ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. SECTION.NAME: PW_DFT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section contains all information to run an SIRIUS PW calculation.

SECTION.NAME: MM
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section contains all information to run a MM calculation.

SECTION.NAME: FORCEFIELD
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Section specifying information regarding how to set up properly a force_field for the classical calculations.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARMTYPE

ITEM.NAME: OFF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Provides force field parameters through the input file

ITEM.NAME: CHM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Provides force field parameters through an external file with CHARMM format

ITEM.NAME: G87
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Provides force field parameters through an external file with GROMOS 87 format

ITEM.NAME: G96
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Provides force field parameters through an external file with GROMOS 96 format

ITEM.NAME: AMBER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Provides force field parameters through an external file with AMBER format (from v.8 on)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Define the kind of torsion potential

KEYWORD.NAME: PARM_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the filename that contains the parameters of the FF.

KEYWORD.NAME: SHIFT_CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Add a constant energy shift to the real-space non-bonding interactions (both Van der Waals and electrostatic) such that the energy at the cutoff radius is zero. This makes the non-bonding interactions continuous at the cutoff.

KEYWORD.NAME: DO_NONBONDED
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Controls the computation of all the real-space (short-range) nonbonded interactions. This also includes the real-space corrections for excluded or scaled 1-2, 1-3 and 1-4 interactions. When set to F, the neighborlists are not created and all interactions that depend on them are not computed.

KEYWORD.NAME: DO_ELECTROSTATICS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Controls the computation of all the real-space (short-range) electrostatics interactions. This does not affect the QM/MM electrostatic coupling when turned off.

KEYWORD.NAME: IGNORE_MISSING_CRITICAL_PARAMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Do not abort when critical force-field parameters are missing. CP2K will run as if the terms containing the missing parameters are zero.

KEYWORD.NAME: MULTIPLE_POTENTIAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Enables the possibility to define NONBONDED and NONBONDED14 as a sum of different kinds of potential. Useful for piecewise defined potentials.

KEYWORD.NAME: ZBL_SCATTERING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A short range repulsive potential is added, to simulate collisions and scattering.

SECTION.NAME: SPLINE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: specifies parameters to set up the splines used in the nonboned interactions (both pair body potential and many body potential)

KEYWORD.NAME: R0_NB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the minimum value of the distance interval that brackets the value of emax_spline.

KEYWORD.NAME: RCUT_NB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Cutoff radius for nonbonded interactions. This value overrides the value specified in the potential definition and is global for all potentials.

KEYWORD.NAME: EMAX_SPLINE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the maximum value of the potential up to which splines will be constructed

KEYWORD.NAME: EMAX_ACCURACY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the maximum value of energy used to check the accuracy requested through EPS_SPLINE. Energy values larger than EMAX_ACCURACY generally do not satisfy the requested accuracy

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_SPLINE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the threshold for the choice of the number of points used in the splines (comparing the splined value with the analytically evaluated one)

KEYWORD.NAME: NPOINTS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Override the default search for an accurate spline by specifying a fixed number of spline points.

KEYWORD.NAME: UNIQUE_SPLINE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: For few potentials (Lennard-Jones) one global optimal spline is generated instead of different optimal splines for each kind of potential

SECTION.NAME: NONBONDED

SECTION.NAME: EAM
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the input parameters for EAM potential type.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kind involved in the nonbond potential

KEYWORD.NAME: PARM_FILE_NAME
PARMFILE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the filename that contains the tabulated EAM potential. File structure: the first line of the potential file contains a title. The second line contains: atomic number, mass and lattice constant. These information are parsed but not used in CP2K. The third line contains: dr: increment of r for the tabulated values of density and phi (assuming r starts in 0) [angstrom]; drho: increment of density for the tabulated values of the embedding function (assuming rho starts in 0) [au_c]; cutoff: cutoff of the EAM potential; npoints: number of points in tabulated. Follow in order npoints lines for rho [au_c] and its derivative [au_c*angstrom^-1]; npoints lines for PHI [ev] and its derivative [ev*angstrom^-1] and npoint lines for the embedded function [ev] and its derivative [ev*au_c^-1].

SECTION.NAME: QUIP
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the input parameters for QUIP potential type. Mainly intended for things like GAP corrections to DFT to achieve correlated-wavefunction-like accuracy. Requires linking with quip library from <http://www.libatoms.org>.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kinds involved in the QUIP potential. For more than 2 elements, &QUIP section must be repeated until each element has been mentioned at least once. Set IGNORE_MISSING_CRITICAL_PARAMS to T in enclosing &FORCEFIELD section to avoid having to list every pair of elements separately.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARM_FILE_NAME
PARMFILE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the filename that contains the QUIP potential.

KEYWORD.NAME: INIT_ARGS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the potential initialization arguments for the QUIP potential. If blank (default) first potential defined in QUIP parameter file will be used.

KEYWORD.NAME: CALC_ARGS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the potential calculation arguments for the QUIP potential.

Mathematical Operators recognized are +, -, *, /, ** or alternatively ^, whereas symbols for brackets must be (). The function parser recognizes the (single argument) Fortran 90 intrinsic functions abs, exp, log10, log, sqrt, sinh, cosh, tanh, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, erf, erfc. Parsing for intrinsic functions is not case sensitive.

SECTION.NAME: SIEPMANN
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the input parameters for the Siepmann-Sprik potential type. Consists of 4 terms: T1+T2+T3+T4. The terms T1=A/rij^alpha and T2=-C/rij^6 have to be given via the GENPOT section. The terms T3+T4 are obtained from the SIEPMANN section. The Siepmann-Sprik potential is designed for water-metal chemisorption.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kind involved in the nonbond potential

KEYWORD.NAME: B
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the B parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: D
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the D parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: E
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the E parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: F
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the F parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: BETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the beta parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: RCUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the cutoff parameter of Siepmann potential

KEYWORD.NAME: ALLOW_OH_FORMATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Siepmann-Sprik potential is actually designed for intact water molecules only. If water is treated at the QM level, water molecules can potentially dissociate, i.e. some O-H bonds might be stretched leading temporarily to the formation of OH- ions. This keyword allows the the formation of such ions. The T3 term (dipole term) is then switched off for evaluating the interaction between the OH- ion and the metal.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALLOW_H3O_FORMATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Siepmann-Sprik potential is designed for intact water molecules only. If water is treated at the QM level and an acid is present, hydronium ions might occur. This keyword allows the formation of hydronium ions. The T3 term (dipole term) is switched off for evaluating the interaction between hydronium and the metal.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALLOW_O_FORMATION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Siepmann-Sprik potential is actually designed for intact water molecules only. If water is treated at the QM level, water molecules can potentially dissociate, i.e. some O-H bonds might be stretched leading temporarily to the formation of O^2- ions. This keyword allows the the formation of such ions. The T3 term (dipole term) is then switched off for evaluating the interaction between the O^2- ion and the metal.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the input parameters for a generic potential type. A functional form is specified. Mathematical Operators recognized are +, -, *, /, ** or alternatively ^, whereas symbols for brackets must be (). The function parser recognizes the (single argument) Fortran 90 intrinsic functions abs, exp, log10, log, sqrt, sinh, cosh, tanh, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, erf, erfc. Parsing for intrinsic functions is not case sensitive.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kind involved in the generic potential

KEYWORD.NAME: FUNCTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the functional form in mathematical notation.

KEYWORD.NAME: VARIABLES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the variable of the functional form.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARAMETERS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the parameters of the functional form

KEYWORD.NAME: VALUES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the values of parameter of the functional form

KEYWORD.NAME: UNITS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Optionally, allows to define valid CP2K unit strings for each parameter value. It is assumed that the corresponding parameter value is specified in this unit.

KEYWORD.NAME: RCUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the cutoff parameter of the generic potential

KEYWORD.NAME: RMIN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the lower bound of the potential. If not set the range is the full range generate by the spline

KEYWORD.NAME: RMAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the upper bound of the potential. If not set the range is the full range generate by the spline

SECTION.NAME: CHARGE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the charge of the MM atoms

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOM
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kind of the charge.

KEYWORD.NAME: CHARGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the charge of the MM atom in electron charge unit.

SECTION.NAME: CHARGES
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Allow to specify an array of classical charges, thus avoiding the packing and permitting the usage of different charges for same atomic types.

DEFAULT_KEYWORD.NAME: DEFAULT_KEYWORD
DEFAULT_KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Value of the charge for the individual atom. Order MUST reflect the one specified for the geometry.

SECTION.NAME: SHELL
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the parameters for shell-model potentials

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: The kind for which the shell potential parameters are given

KEYWORD.NAME: CORE_CHARGE
CORE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Partial charge assigned to the core (electron charge units)

KEYWORD.NAME: SHELL_CHARGE
SHELL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Partial charge assigned to the shell (electron charge units)

KEYWORD.NAME: MASS_FRACTION
MASS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fraction of the mass of the atom to be assigned to the shell

KEYWORD.NAME: K2_SPRING
K2
SPRING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Force constant k2 of the spring potential 1/2*k2*r^2 + 1/24*k4*r^4 binding a core-shell pair when a core-shell potential is employed.

KEYWORD.NAME: K4_SPRING
K4
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Force constant k4 of the spring potential 1/2*k2*r^2 + 1/24*k4*r^4 binding a core-shell pair when a core-shell potential is employed. By default a harmonic spring potential is used, i.e. k4 is zero.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_DISTANCE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Assign a maximum elongation of the spring, if negative no limit is imposed

KEYWORD.NAME: SHELL_CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Define a screening function to exclude some neighbors of the shell when electrostatic interaction are considered, if negative no screening is operated

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kinds involved in the bond.

ITEM.NAME: HARMONIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (HARMONIC|G87): 1/2*K*(R-R0)^2

ITEM.NAME: CHARMM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CHARMM|AMBER): K*(R-R0)^2

ITEM.NAME: AMBER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CHARMM|AMBER): K*(R-R0)^2

ITEM.NAME: G87
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (HARMONIC|G87): 1/2*K*(R-R0)^2

ITEM.NAME: G96
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (G96): 1/4*K*(R^2-R0^2)^2

ITEM.NAME: QUARTIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (QUARTIC): (1/2*K1+[1/3*K2+1/4*K3*|R-R0|]*|R-R0|)(R-R0)^2

ITEM.NAME: MORSE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (MORSE): K1*[(1-exp(-K2*(R-R0)))^2-1])

ITEM.NAME: CUBIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CUBIC): K*(R-R0)^2*(1+cs*(R-R0)+7/12*(cs^2*(R-R0)^2))

ITEM.NAME: FUES
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (FUES): 1/2*K*R0^2*(1+R0/R*(R0/R-2))

KEYWORD.NAME: K
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the force constant of the potential. For MORSE potentials 2 numbers are expected. For QUARTIC potentials 3 numbers are expected.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the bend potential of the MM system.

KEYWORD.NAME: ATOMS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the atomic kinds involved in the bend.

KEYWORD.NAME: KIND

ITEM.NAME: HARMONIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (HARMONIC|G87): 1/2*K*(THETA-THETA0)^2

ITEM.NAME: CHARMM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CHARMM|AMBER): K*(THETA-THETA0)^2

ITEM.NAME: AMBER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CHARMM|AMBER): K*(THETA-THETA0)^2

ITEM.NAME: G87
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (HARMONIC|G87): 1/2*K*(THETA-THETA0)^2

ITEM.NAME: G96
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (G96): 1/2*K*(COS(THETA)-THETA0)^2

ITEM.NAME: CUBIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (CUBIC): K*(THETA-THETA0)**2*(1+CB*(THETA-THETA0))

ITEM.NAME: MIXED_BEND_STRETCH
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (MIXED_BEND_STRETCH): K*(THETA-THETA0)**2*(1+CB*(THETA-THETA0))+ KSS*(R12-R012)*(R32-R032)+KBS12*(R12-R012)*(THETA-THETA0)+KBS32*(R32-R032)*(THETA-THETA0)

ITEM.NAME: MM3
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (MM3): 1/2*K*(THETA-THETA0)**2*(1-0.014*(THETA-THETA0)+5.6E-5*(THETA-THETA0)**2 -7.0E-7*(THETA-THETA0)**3+9.0E-10*(THETA-THETA0)**4)+KBS12*(R12-R012)*(THETA-THETA0)+ KBS32*(R32-R032)*(THETA-THETA0)

ITEM.NAME: LEGENDRE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Functional Form (LEGENDRE): sum_{i=0}^N c_i*P_i(COS(THETA))

KEYWORD.NAME: CB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the the cubic force constant of the bend

KEYWORD.NAME: LEGENDRE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the coefficients for the legendre expansion of the bending potential. 'THETA0' and 'K' are not used, but need to be specified. Use an arbitrary value.

SECTION.NAME: NEIGHBOR_LISTS
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies the input parameters for the construction of neighbor lists.

KEYWORD.NAME: VERLET_SKIN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the Verlet Skin for the generation of the neighbor lists

KEYWORD.NAME: NEIGHBOR_LISTS_FROM_SCRATCH
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword enables the building of the neighbouring list from scratch.

KEYWORD.NAME: GEO_CHECK
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword enables the check that two atoms are never below the minimum value used to construct the splines during the construction of the neighbouring list. Disabling this keyword avoids CP2K to abort in case two atoms are below the minimum value of the radius used to generate the splines.

KEYWORD.NAME: POISSON_SOLVER
POISSON
PSOLVER

ITEM.NAME: PERIODIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: PERIODIC is only available for fully (3D) periodic systems.

ITEM.NAME: ANALYTIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: ANALYTIC is available for 0D, 1D and 2D periodic solutions using analytical green functions in the g space (slow convergence).

ITEM.NAME: MT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: MT (Martyna Tuckermann) decoupling that interacts only with the nearest neighbor. Beware results are completely wrong if the cell is smaller than twice the cluster size (with electronic density). Available for 0D and 2D systems.

ITEM.NAME: MULTIPOLE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: MULTIPOLE uses a scheme that fits the total charge with one gaussian per atom. Available only for cluster (0D) systems.

ITEM.NAME: WAVELET
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: WAVELET allows for 0D, 2D (but only PERIODIC XZ) and 3D systems. It does not require very large unit cells, only that the density goes to zero on the faces of the cell. The use of PREFERRED_FFT_LIBRARY FFTSG is required.

ITEM.NAME: IMPLICIT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: IMPLICIT allows for 0D, 1D, 2D and 3D systems.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify which kind of solver to use to solve the Poisson equation.

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the directions in which PBC apply. Important notice, this only applies to the electrostatics. See the CELL section to specify the periodicity used for e.g. the pair lists. Typically the settings should be the same.

SECTION.NAME: MT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up parameters of Martyna-Tuckerman poisson solver. Note that exact results are only guaranteed if the unit cell is twice as large as charge density (and serious artefacts can result if the cell is much smaller).

KEYWORD.NAME: REL_CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the multiplicative factor for the CUTOFF keyword in MULTI_GRID section. The result gives the cutoff at which the 1/r non-periodic FFT3D is evaluated. Default is 2.0

SECTION.NAME: WAVELET
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Sets up parameters of wavelet based poisson solver.

KEYWORD.NAME: SCF_TYPE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Type of scaling function used in the wavelet approach, the total energy depends on this choice, and the convergence with respect to cutoff depends on the selected scaling functions. Possible values are 8,14,16,20,24,30,40,50,60,100

SECTION.NAME: MULTIPOLE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section is used to set up the decoupling of QM periodic images with the use of density derived atomic point charges.

KEYWORD.NAME: RCUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Real space cutoff for the Ewald sum.

KEYWORD.NAME: EWALD_PRECISION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Precision achieved in the Ewald sum.

KEYWORD.NAME: ANALYTICAL_GTERM
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Evaluates the Gterm in the Ewald Scheme analytically instead of using Splines.

KEYWORD.NAME: NGRIDS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the number of grid points used for the Interpolation of the G-space term

SECTION.NAME: INTERPOLATOR
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: controls the interpolation for the G-space term

KEYWORD.NAME: AINT_PRECOND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: the approximate inverse to use to get the starting point for the linear solver of the spline3 methods

KEYWORD.NAME: PRECOND
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The preconditioner used for the linear solver of the spline3 methods

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_X
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: accuracy on the solution for spline3 the interpolators

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_R
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: accuracy on the residual for spline3 the interpolators

SECTION.NAME: CONV_INFO
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: if convergence information about the linear solver of the spline methods should be printed

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: EWALD
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Ewald parameters controlling electrostatic only for CLASSICAL MM.

KEYWORD.NAME: EWALD_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: NONE standard real-space coulomb potential is computed together with the non-bonded contributions

ITEM.NAME: EWALD
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: EWALD is the standard non-fft based ewald

ITEM.NAME: PME
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: PME is the particle mesh using fft interpolation

ITEM.NAME: SPME
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: SPME is the smooth particle mesh using beta-Euler splines (recommended)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The type of ewald you want to perform.

KEYWORD.NAME: EWALD_ACCURACY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Expected accuracy in the Ewald sum. This number affects only the calculation of the cutoff for the real-space term of the ewald summation (EWALD|PME|SPME) as well as the construction of the neighbor lists (if the cutoff for non-bonded terms is smaller than the value employed to compute the EWALD real-space term). This keyword has no effect on the reciprocal space term (which can be tuned independently).

KEYWORD.NAME: RCUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Explicitly provide the real-space cutoff of the ewald summation (EWALD|PME|SPME). This value is ignored in Tight-binding applications (rcut from basis overlap is used). If present, overwrites the estimate of EWALD_ACCURACY and may affect the construction of the neighbor lists for non-bonded terms (in FIST), if the value specified is larger than the cutoff for non-bonded interactions.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: alpha parameter associated with Ewald (EWALD|PME|SPME). Recommended for small systems is alpha = 3.5 / r_cut. For Tight-binding application a recommended value is alpha = 1.0. Tuning alpha, r_cut and gmax is needed to obtain O(N**1.5) scaling for ewald.

KEYWORD.NAME: GMAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: number of grid points (SPME and EWALD). If a single number is specified, the same number of points is used for all three directions on the grid. If three numbers are given, each direction can have a different number of points. The number of points needs to be FFTable (which depends on the library used) and odd for EWALD. The optimal number depends e.g. on alpha and the size of the cell. 1 point per Angstrom is common.

KEYWORD.NAME: NS_MAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: number of grid points on small mesh (PME only), should be odd.

KEYWORD.NAME: O_SPLINE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: order of the beta-Euler spline (SPME only)

KEYWORD.NAME: EPSILON
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: tolerance of gaussians for fft interpolation (PME only)

SECTION.NAME: RS_GRID
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Set options that influence how the realspace grids are being distributed in parallel runs.

ITEM.NAME: AUTOMATIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use heuristic rules to decide between distributed and replicated

ITEM.NAME: DISTRIBUTED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Force a distributed setup if possible

ITEM.NAME: REPLICATED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Force a replicated setup

KEYWORD.NAME: DISTRIBUTION_LAYOUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the number of slices in the x, y and z directions. -1 specifies that any number of slices is OK. If a given distribution can not be satisfied, a replicated grid will result. Also see LOCK_DISTRIBUTION.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_DISTRIBUTED_LEVEL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the multigrid-level of a grid is larger than the parameter, it will not be distributed in the automatic scheme.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOCK_DISTRIBUTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Expert use only, only basic QS deals correctly with a non-default value. If the distribution is locked, a grid will have the same distribution as the next finer multigrid (provided it is distributed). If unlocked, all grids can be distributed freely.

KEYWORD.NAME: MEMORY_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A grid will only be distributed if the memory usage for that grid (including halo) is smaller than a replicated grid by this parameter.

KEYWORD.NAME: HALO_REDUCTION_FACTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Can be used to reduce the halo of the distributed grid (experimental features).

SECTION.NAME: MULTIPOLES
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Enables the use of multipoles in the treatment of the electrostatics.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Controls the activation of the Multipoles

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_MULTIPOLE_EXPANSION

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No multipolar terms! Check the codes providing a zero contribution.

ITEM.NAME: CHARGE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use up to the Charge term

ITEM.NAME: DIPOLE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use up to the Dipole term

ITEM.NAME: QUADRUPOLE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use up to the Quadrupole term

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the maximum level of multipoles expansion used for the electrostatics.

KEYWORD.NAME: POL_SCF

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No inducible multipoles.

ITEM.NAME: SELF_CONSISTENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Conventional self-consistent iteration.

ITEM.NAME: CONJUGATE_GRADIENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Linear conjugate-gradient optimization of the sum of the electrostatic and induction energy. This method does not support non-linear polarization but is sometimes faster.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the method to obtain self consistent induced multipole moments.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_IPOL_ITER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the maximum number of iterations for induced dipoles

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_POL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the rmsd threshold for the derivatives of the energy towards the Cartesian dipoles components

SECTION.NAME: PROGRAM_RUN_INFO
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: controls the printing of ewald setup

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.NAME: IMPLICIT
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for the implicit (generalized) Poisson solver.

KEYWORD.NAME: BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS

ITEM.NAME: PERIODIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: periodic boundary conditions

ITEM.NAME: MIXED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Dirichlet + homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions

ITEM.NAME: MIXED_PERIODIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Dirichlet + periodic boundary conditions

ITEM.NAME: NEUMANN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: homogeneous Neumann BC (zero-average solution)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the type of boundary conditions. Dirichlet=fixed value, Neumann=zero normal deriv. Mixed and Neumann boundaries essentially requires FFTW3 so that all grid sizes are FFT-able.

KEYWORD.NAME: ZERO_INITIAL_GUESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to use zero potential as initial guess.

KEYWORD.NAME: OR_PARAMETER
OMEGA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Over-relaxation parameter (large epsilon requires smaller omega ~0.1).

KEYWORD.NAME: NEUMANN_DIRECTIONS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Directions in which homogeneous Neumann conditions are imposed. In the remaining directions periodic conditions will be enforced. Having specified MIXED or NEUMANN as BOUNDARY_CONDITIONS, the keyword is meant to be used to combine periodic and homogeneous Neumann conditions at the boundaries of the simulation cell.

SECTION.NAME: DIELECTRIC
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for the dielectric constant function.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIELECTRIC_CORE_CORRECTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Avoid spurious values of the dielectric constant at the ionic core for pseudopotentials where the electron density goes to zero at the core (e.g. GTH). The correction is based on rho_core.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIELECTRIC_FUNCTION_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: DENSITY_DEPENDENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Dielectric constant as a function of the electron density as e.g. proposed within the SCCS model.

ITEM.NAME: SPATIALLY_DEPENDENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Various regions with different dielectric constants.

ITEM.NAME: SPATIALLY_RHO_DEPENDENT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Various regions with different dielectric constants. The dielectric constant decays to 1.0, wherever the electron density is present.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preferred type for the dielectric constant function.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT
EPSILON
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Dielectric constant in the bulk of the solvent.

KEYWORD.NAME: DERIVATIVE_METHOD

ITEM.NAME: FFT
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: FFT based deriv of epsilon, without correction (high cutoff needed).

ITEM.NAME: FFT_USE_DEPS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: FFT based deriv of epsilon, with correction using gradient of epsilon (high cutoff needed).

ITEM.NAME: FFT_USE_DRHO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: FFT based deriv of epsilon, with correction using gradient of rho (high cutoff needed).

ITEM.NAME: CD3
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 3-point central difference derivative.

ITEM.NAME: CD5
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 5-point central difference derivative.

ITEM.NAME: CD7
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: 7-point central difference derivative (recommended).

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Preferred method for evaluating the gradient of ln(eps).

SECTION.NAME: DIELEC_AA_CUBOIDAL
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating axis-aligned cuboidal dielectric region. Note that once such a region is defined, the 'background' dielectric constant would be the default (80.0), unless a different value is specified using the keyword IMPLICIT%DIELECTRIC%DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT
EPSILON
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: value of the dielectric constant inside the region.

KEYWORD.NAME: X_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The X extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: Y_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Y extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: Z_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Z extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
ZETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the standard mollifier.

SECTION.NAME: DIELEC_XAA_ANNULAR
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating x-axis-aligned annular dielectric region. Note that once such a region is defined, the 'background' dielectric constant would be the default (80.0), unless a different value is specified using the keyword IMPLICIT%DIELECTRIC%DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT.

KEYWORD.NAME: DIELECTRIC_CONSTANT
EPSILON
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: value of the dielectric constant inside the region.

KEYWORD.NAME: X_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The X extents of the annulus.

KEYWORD.NAME: BASE_CENTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The y and z coordinates of the annulus' base center.

KEYWORD.NAME: BASE_RADII
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The base radius of the annulus.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
ZETA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the standard mollifier.

SECTION.NAME: DIRICHLET_BC
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating Dirichlet type boundary conditions.

KEYWORD.NAME: VERBOSE_OUTPUT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Print out the coordinates of the vertices defining Dirichlet regions and their tessellations (in Angstrom), the values of the electrostatic potential at the regions (in a.u.), and their corresponding evaluated Lagrange multipliers.

SECTION.NAME: AA_PLANAR
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating axis-aligned planar (rectangular) Dirichlet boundary regions.

KEYWORD.NAME: V_D
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The value of the fixed potential to be imposed at the axis-aligned Dirichlet boundary.

KEYWORD.NAME: OSCILLATING_FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A fraction of the field can be set to oscilate over time.

KEYWORD.NAME: FREQUENCY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The frequency with which the oscillating fraction oscillates.

KEYWORD.NAME: PHASE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The phase of the oscillattion. A phase of zero corresponds to a cosine function.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARALLEL_PLANE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The coordinate plane that the region is parallel to.

KEYWORD.NAME: INTERCEPT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The intercept of the rectangle's plane.

KEYWORD.NAME: X_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The X extents of the rectangle.

KEYWORD.NAME: Y_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Y extents of the rectangle.

KEYWORD.NAME: Z_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Z extents of the rectangle.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_PRTN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of partitions in the directions of the unit vectors generating the corresponding PARALLEL_PLANE (e1, e2 or e3) for tiling the rectangluar region.

KEYWORD.NAME: THICKNESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The thickness of the planar Dirichlet region.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
SIGMA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the transition region between the Dirichlet subdomain and its surrounding.

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC_REGION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to take into consideration the effects of the periodicity of the simulation cell (MIXED_PERIODIC bc) for regions defined sufficiently close to the boundaries.

SECTION.NAME: PLANAR
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating planar (rectangular) Dirichlet boundary regions with given vertices.

KEYWORD.NAME: V_D
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The value of the fixed potential to be imposed at the planar Dirichlet boundary.

KEYWORD.NAME: OSCILLATING_FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A fraction of the field can be set to oscilate over time.

KEYWORD.NAME: FREQUENCY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The frequency with which the oscillating fraction oscillates.

KEYWORD.NAME: PHASE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The phase of the oscillattion. A phase of zero corresponds to a cosine function.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_PRTN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of partitions along the edges for tiling the rectangular region. If the edges have different lengths, from the two given values, the larger one will be assigned to the longer edge.

KEYWORD.NAME: THICKNESS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The thickness of the planar Dirichlet region.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
SIGMA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the transition region between the Dirichlet subdomain and its surrounding.

SECTION.NAME: AA_CYLINDRICAL
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating axis-aligned cylindrical Dirichlet boundary regions.

KEYWORD.NAME: V_D
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The value of the fixed potential to be imposed at the cylindrical Dirichlet boundary.

KEYWORD.NAME: OSCILLATING_FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A fraction of the field can be set to oscilate over time.

KEYWORD.NAME: FREQUENCY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The frequency with which the oscillating fraction oscillates.

KEYWORD.NAME: PHASE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The phase of the oscillattion. A phase of zero corresponds to a cosine function.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARALLEL_AXIS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The coordinate axis that the cylindrical region extends along.

KEYWORD.NAME: XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The extents of the cylinder along its central axis.

KEYWORD.NAME: BASE_CENTER
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The y and z coordinates (x and z or x and y coordinates, depending on the choice of the parallel axis) of the cylinder's base center.

KEYWORD.NAME: BASE_RADIUS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The base radius of the cylinder.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_SIDES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of sides (faces) of the n-gonal prism approximating the cylinder.

KEYWORD.NAME: APX_TYPE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the type of the n-gonal prism approximating the cylinder.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_PRTN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of partitions along the face edges of the prism for tiling. If the edges have different lengths, from the two given values, the larger one will be assigned to the longer edge.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
SIGMA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the transition region between the Dirichlet subdomain and its surrounding.

KEYWORD.NAME: DELTA_ALPHA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A central angle specifying the gap between the faces of the n-gonal prism. To avoide overlap between the cuboids (of the given thickness) built on top of the faces, a larger value is required if the number of faces (N_SIDES) is quite few and/or the base radius is fairly small.

SECTION.NAME: AA_CUBOIDAL
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Parameters for creating axis-aligned cuboidal Dirichlet regions.

KEYWORD.NAME: V_D
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The value of the fixed potential to be imposed at the region.

KEYWORD.NAME: OSCILLATING_FRACTION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: A fraction of the field can be set to oscilate over time.

KEYWORD.NAME: FREQUENCY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The frequency with which the oscillating fraction oscillates.

KEYWORD.NAME: PHASE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The phase of the oscillattion. A phase of zero corresponds to a cosine function.

KEYWORD.NAME: X_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The X extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: Y_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Y extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: Z_XTNT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The Z extents of the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: N_PRTN
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The number of partitions in the x, y and z directions for partitioning the cuboid.

KEYWORD.NAME: SMOOTHING_WIDTH
SIGMA
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The width of the transition region between the Dirichlet subdomain and its surrounding.

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC_REGION
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Whether or not to take into consideration the effects of the periodicity of the simulation cell (MIXED_PERIODIC bc) for regions defined sufficiently close to the boundaries.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: parameters for finite periodic electric field computed using the Berry phase approach. IMPORTANT: Can only be used in combination with OT. Can not be used in combination with RTP or EMD, e.g. RESTART_RTP has to be .FALSE. when restarting the job.

SECTION.NAME: DIPOLE
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Section controlling the calculation of DIPOLE. Note that the result in the periodic case might be defined modulo a certain period, determined by the lattice vectors. During MD, this can lead to jumps.

SECTION_PARAMETERS.NAME: SECTION_PARAMETERS
SECTION_PARAMETERS.DESCRIPTION: Level starting at which this property is printed

KEYWORD.NAME: __CONTROL_VAL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: hidden parameter that controls storage, printing,... of the print_key

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Use Berry phase formula (PERIODIC=T) or simple operator (PERIODIC=F). The latter normally requires that the CELL is periodic NONE.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFERENCE
REF

ITEM.NAME: COM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Mass

ITEM.NAME: COAC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Center of Atomic Charges

ITEM.NAME: USER_DEFINED
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use User Defined Point (Keyword:REF_POINT)

ITEM.NAME: ZERO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Use Origin of Coordinate System

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Define the reference point for the calculation of the electrostatic moment.

KEYWORD.NAME: REFERENCE_POINT
REF_POINT
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Fixed reference point for the calculations of the electrostatic moment.

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Section to bias the committee disagreement (sigma) by E = 0.5 * K_B * (sigma - SIGMA_0)**2, if sigma > SIGMA_0.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Remove PES shifts within the committee by subtracting energy for each committee member. Provide one number per C-NNP member.

KEYWORD.NAME: ADD_LAST

ITEM.NAME: NO
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Do not mark last iteration specifically

ITEM.NAME: NUMERIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with its iteration number

ITEM.NAME: SYMBOLIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mark last iteration with lowercase letter l

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: If the last iteration should be added, and if it should be marked symbolically (with lowercase letter l) or with the iteration number. Not every iteration level is able to identify the last iteration early enough to be able to output. When this keyword is activated all iteration levels are checked for the last iteration step.

KEYWORD.NAME: COMMON_ITERATION_LEVELS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How many iterations levels should be written in the same file (no extra information about the actual iteration level is written to the file)

KEYWORD.NAME: FILENAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: controls part of the filename for output. use __STD_OUT__ (exactly as written here) for the screen or standard logger. use filename to obtain projectname-filename. use ./filename to get filename. A middle name (if present), iteration numbers and extension are always added to the filename. if you want to avoid it use =filename, in this case the filename is always exactly as typed. Please note that this can lead to clashes of filenames.

KEYWORD.NAME: LOG_PRINT_KEY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keywords enables the logger for the print_key (a message is printed on screen everytime data, controlled by this print_key, are written)

SECTION.NAME: EACH
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section specifies how often this property is printed. Each keyword inside this section is mapping to a specific iteration level and the value of each of these keywords is matched with the iteration level during the calculation. How to handle the last iteration is treated separately in ADD_LAST (this mean that each iteration level (MD, GEO_OPT, etc..), though equal to 0, might print the last iteration). If an iteration level is specified that is not present in the flow of the calculation it is just ignored.

KEYWORD.NAME: E_COUPL
QMMM_COUPLING
ECOUPL

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Mechanical coupling (i.e. classical point charge based)

ITEM.NAME: COULOMB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using analytical 1/r potential (Coulomb) - not available for GPW/GAPW

ITEM.NAME: GAUSS
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using fast gaussian expansion of the electrostatic potential (Erf(r/rc)/r) - not available for DFTB.

ITEM.NAME: S-WAVE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using fast gaussian expansion of the s-wave electrostatic potential

ITEM.NAME: POINT_CHARGE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Using quantum mechanics derived point charges interacting with MM charges

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the type of the QM - MM electrostatic coupling.

KEYWORD.NAME: MM_POTENTIAL_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Name of the file containing the potential expansion in gaussians. See the USE_GEEP_LIB keyword.

KEYWORD.NAME: USE_GEEP_LIB
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword enables the use of the internal GEEP library to generate the gaussian expansion of the MM potential. Using this keyword there's no need to provide the MM_POTENTIAL_FILENAME. It expects a number from 2 to 15 (the number of gaussian functions to be used in the expansion.

KEYWORD.NAME: NOCOMPATIBILITY
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword disables the compatibility of QM/MM potential between CPMD and CP2K implementations. The compatibility is achieved using an MM potential of the form: Erf[x/rc]/x + (1/rc -2/(pi^1/2*rc))*Exp[-(x/rc)^2]. This keyword has effect only selecting GAUSS E_COUPLING type.

KEYWORD.NAME: EPS_MM_RSPACE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Set the threshold for the collocation of the GEEP gaussian functions. this keyword affects only the GAUSS E_COUPLING.

KEYWORD.NAME: SPHERICAL_CUTOFF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Set the spherical cutoff for the QMMM electrostatic interaction. This acts like a charge multiplicative factor dependent on cutoff. For MM atoms farther than the SPHERICAL_CUTOFF(1) their charge is zero. The switch is performed with a smooth function: 0.5*(1-TANH((r-[SPH_CUT(1)-20*SPH_CUT(2)])/(SPH_CUT(2)))). Two values are required: the first one is the distance cutoff. The second one controls the stiffness of the smoothing.

KEYWORD.NAME: PARALLEL_SCHEME

ITEM.NAME: ATOM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: parallelizes on atoms. grids replicated. Replication of the grids can be quite expensive memory wise if running on a system with limited memory per core. The grid option may be preferred in this case.

ITEM.NAME: GRID
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: parallelizes on grid slices. atoms replicated.

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Chooses the parallel_scheme for the long range Potential

ITEM.NAME: EVERY_STEP

ITEM.NAME: SETUP_ONLY
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Center at first step only

ITEM.NAME: NEVER

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword sets when the QM system is automatically centered. Default is EVERY_STEP.

ITEM.NAME: MAX_MINUS_MIN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Center of box defined by maximum coordinate minus minimum coordinate

ITEM.NAME: PBC_AWARE_MAX_MINUS_MIN
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: PBC-aware centering (useful for &QMMM&FORCE_MIXING)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword specifies how to do the QM system centering.

KEYWORD.NAME: CENTER_GRID
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword specifies whether the QM system is centered in units of the grid spacing.

KEYWORD.NAME: INITIAL_TRANSLATION_VECTOR
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: This keyword specify the initial translation vector to be applied to the system.

KEYWORD.NAME: DELTA_CHARGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Additional net charge relative to that specified in DFT section. Used automatically by force mixing

SECTION.NAME: FORCE_MIXING
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: This section enables and defines parameters for force-mixing based QM/MM, which actually does two conventional QM/MM calculations, on a small and a large QM region, and combines the MM forces from one and QM forces from the other to create a complete set of forces. Energy is not conserved (although the QM/MM energy from the large QM region calculation is reported) so a proper thermostat (i.e. massive, and able to handle dissipation, such as Adaptive Langevin (AD_LANGEVIN)) must be used. For some propagation algorithms (NVT and REFTRAJ MD ensembles) algorithm is adaptive, including molecules hysteretically based on their instantaneous distance from the core region. Information on core/QM/buffer labels can be written in PDB file using MOTION&PRINT&FORCE_MIXING_LABELS. Will fail if calculation requires a meaningfull stress, or an energy that is consistent with the forces. For GEO_OPT this means only MOTION&GEO_OPT&TYPE CG, MOTION&GEO_OPT&CG&LINE_SEARCH&TYPE 2PNT, and MOTION&GEO_OPT&CG&LINE_SEARCH&2PNT&LINMIN_GRAD_ONLY T

KEYWORD.NAME: MOMENTUM_CONSERVATION_TYPE

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No momentum conservation

ITEM.NAME: EQUAL_F
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Equal force on each atom

ITEM.NAME: EQUAL_A
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Equal acceleration on each atom

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: How to apply force to get momentum conservation

KEYWORD.NAME: MOMENTUM_CONSERVATION_REGION

ITEM.NAME: CORE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Apply to QM core region

ITEM.NAME: QM
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Apply to full QM (dynamics) region

ITEM.NAME: BUFFER
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Apply to QM+buffer regions

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Region to apply correction force to for momentum conservation

KEYWORD.NAME: R_CORE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the inner and outer radii of core QM region. All molecules with any atoms within this distance (hysteretically) of any atoms specified as QM in enclosing QM/MM section will be core QM atoms in the force-mixing calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: R_QM
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the inner and outer radii of QM dynamics region. All molecules with atoms within this distance (hysteretically) of any atoms in core will follow QM dynamics in the force-mixing calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: QM_EXTENDED_SEED_IS_ONLY_CORE_LIST
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Makes the extended QM zone be defined hysterestically by distance from QM core list (i.e. atoms specified explicitly by user) instead of from full QM core region (specified by user + hysteretic selection + unbreakable bonds)

KEYWORD.NAME: R_BUF
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the inner and outer radii of buffer region. All atoms within this distance (hysteretically) of any QM atoms will be buffer atoms in the force-mixing calculation.

KEYWORD.NAME: QM_KIND_ELEMENT_MAPPING
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Mapping from elements to QM_KINDs for adaptively included atoms.

KEYWORD.NAME: MAX_N_QM
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Maximum number of QM atoms, for detection of runaway adaptive selection.

KEYWORD.NAME: ADAPTIVE_EXCLUDE_MOLECULES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: List of molecule names to exclude from adaptive regions (e.g. big things like proteins)

KEYWORD.NAME: EXTENDED_DELTA_CHARGE
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Additional net charge in extended region relative to core (core charge is specified in DFT section, as usual for a convetional QM/MM calculation)

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: List of atoms always in QM region, non-adaptively

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the scaling factor to be used for projecting the forces on the capping hydrogen in the IMOMM QM/MM link scheme to the MM atom of the link. A good guess can be derived from the bond distances of the forcefield: alpha = r_eq(QM-MM) / r_eq(QM-H).

KEYWORD.NAME: FIST_SCALE_FACTOR

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: The indexes of the MM atoms that have this kind. This keyword can be repeated several times (useful if you have to specify many indexes).

SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Information about the MM kind in the QM/MM scheme

KEYWORD.NAME: RADIUS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the radius of the atomic kinds

KEYWORD.NAME: CORR_RADIUS
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the correction radius of the atomic kinds The correction radius is connected to the use of the compatibility keyword.

SECTION.NAME: CELL
SECTION.DESCRIPTION: Input parameters needed to set up the simulation cell. Simple products and fractions combined with functions of a single number can be used like 2/3, 0.3*COS(60) or -SQRT(3)/2. The functions COS, EXP, LOG, LOG10, SIN, SQRT, and TAN are available.

KEYWORD.NAME: A
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the Cartesian components for the cell vector A. This defines the first column of the h matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: B
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the Cartesian components for the cell vector B. This defines the second column of the h matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: C
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the Cartesian components for the cell vector C. This defines the third column of the h matrix.

KEYWORD.NAME: ABC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the lengths of the cell vectors A, B, and C, which defines the diagonal elements of h matrix for an orthorhombic cell. For non-orthorhombic cells it is possible either to specify the angles ALPHA, BETA, GAMMA via ALPHA_BETA_GAMMA keyword or alternatively use the keywords A, B, and C. The convention is that A lies along the X-axis, B is in the XY plane.

KEYWORD.NAME: ALPHA_BETA_GAMMA
ANGLES
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the angles between the vectors A, B and C when using the ABC keyword. The convention is that A lies along the X-axis, B is in the XY plane. ALPHA is the angle between B and C, BETA is the angle between A and C and GAMMA the angle between A and B.

KEYWORD.NAME: CELL_FILE_NAME
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Possibility to read the cell from an external file

KEYWORD.NAME: CELL_FILE_FORMAT

ITEM.NAME: CP2K
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cell info in the CP2K native format.

ITEM.NAME: CIF
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cell info from CIF file.

ITEM.NAME: XSC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cell info in the XSC format (NAMD)

KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the format of the cell file (if used)

KEYWORD.NAME: PERIODIC
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specify the directions for which periodic boundary conditions (PBC) will be applied. Important notice: This applies to the generation of the pair lists as well as to the application of the PBCs to positions. See the POISSON section to specify the periodicity used for the electrostatics. Typically the settings should be the same.

KEYWORD.NAME: MULTIPLE_UNIT_CELL
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the numbers of repetition in space (X, Y, Z) of the defined cell, assuming it as a unit cell. This keyword affects only the CELL specification. The same keyword in SUBSYS%TOPOLOGY%MULTIPLE_UNIT_CELL should be modified in order to affect the coordinates specification.

ITEM.NAME: NONE
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: No cell symmetry

ITEM.NAME: TRICLINIC

ITEM.NAME: MONOCLINIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Monoclinic (a ≠ b ≠ c, α = γ = 90°, β ≠ 90°)

ITEM.NAME: MONOCLINIC_GAMMA_AB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Monoclinic (a = b ≠ c, α = β = 90°, γ ≠ 90°)

ITEM.NAME: ORTHORHOMBIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Orthorhombic (a ≠ b ≠ c, α = β = γ = 90°)

ITEM.NAME: TETRAGONAL_AB
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Tetragonal (a = b ≠ c, α = β = γ = 90°)

ITEM.NAME: TETRAGONAL_AC

ITEM.NAME: TETRAGONAL_BC

ITEM.NAME: TETRAGONAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Tetragonal (alias for TETRAGONAL_AB)

ITEM.NAME: RHOMBOHEDRAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Rhombohedral (a = b = c, α = β = γ ≠ 90°)

ITEM.NAME: HEXAGONAL
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Hexagonal (alias for HEXAGONAL_GAMMA_60)

ITEM.NAME: CUBIC
ITEM.DESCRIPTION: Cubic (a = b = c, α = β = γ = 90°)

KEYWORD.NAME: GMAX
KEYWORD.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the maximum value of G in the reciprocal space over which perform the Ewald sum.
